;;; the Free Software Foundation; either version 3 of the License, or (at
;;; your option) any later version.
;;;
;;; GNU Guix is distributed in the hope that it will be useful, but
;;; WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
;;; MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the
;;; GNU General Public License for more details.
;;;
;;; You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
;;; along with GNU Guix.  If not, see <http://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
(define-module (gnu services games)
#:use-module (gnu services)
#:use-module (gnu services shepherd)
#:use-module (gnu packages admin)
#:use-module (gnu packages games)
#:use-module (gnu system shadow)
#:use-module (guix gexp)
#:use-module (guix modules)
#:use-module (guix records)
#:use-module (ice-9 match)
#:export (wesnothd-configuration
wesnothd-configuration?
wesnothd-service-type))
;;;
;;; The Battle for Wesnoth server
;;;
(define-record-type* <wesnothd-configuration>
wesnothd-configuration make-wesnothd-configuration wesnothd-configuration?
(package wesnothd-configuration-package
(default wesnoth-server))
(port wesnothd-configuration-port
(default 15000)))
(define %wesnothd-accounts
(list (user-account
(name "wesnothd")
(group "wesnothd")
(system? #t)
(comment "Wesnoth daemon user")
(home-directory "/var/empty")
(shell (file-append shadow "/sbin/nologin")))
(user-group
(name "wesnothd")
(system? #t))))
(define wesnothd-shepherd-service
(match-lambda
(($ <wesnothd-configuration> package port)
(with-imported-modules (source-module-closure
'((gnu build shepherd)))
(shepherd-service
(documentation "The Battle for Wesnoth server")
(provision '(wesnoth-daemon))
(requirement '(networking))
(modules '((gnu build shepherd)))
(start #~(make-forkexec-constructor/container
(list #$(file-append package "/bin/wesnothd")
"-p" #$(number->string port))
#:user "wesnothd" #:group "wesnothd"))
(stop #~(make-kill-destructor)))))))
(define wesnothd-service-type
(service-type
(name 'wesnothd)
(description
"Run The Battle for Wesnoth server @command{wesnothd}.")
(extensions
(list (service-extension account-service-type
(const %wesnothd-accounts))
(service-extension shepherd-root-service-typ

data.title: Seed7 – Extensible Programming Language
data.author: 0x54MUR41
data.article_summary: Seed7是一种由Thomas Mertes设计的高级编程语言，具备开源解释器和编译器，编译器将Seed7程序转换为C程序并编译为机器码。Seed7支持用户自定义语句和操作符，具有无特殊语法即可定义模板和泛型的能力。它采用静态类型检查，无自动类型转换，提升编译时错误检测能力。Seed7具备自动内存管理，无需垃圾回收，支持异常处理和源码调试。它提供大整数和大有理数类型，支持函数、操作符和语句的重载。预定义多种数据类型和数据库独立API，可连接多种数据库。Seed7代码具有良好的可移植性，适用于Linux、Unix和Windows系统。解释器和示例程序使用GPL许可，运行库使用LGPL许可。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Seed7编程语言的特性、设计选择及社区反馈

不同观点：
• OtomotO认为Seed7的创造者非常友善且聪明，语言设计精巧，但Seed7过于小众，令人感到遗憾。
• helix278作为一个函数式编程和抽象数据类型（ADT）的爱好者，赞赏Seed7的内存管理和灵活的语法，认为其设计决策优于C++。具体优点包括：1) 限制内存分配和引用，减少内存管理问题；2) 语法灵活，支持更高层次的抽象。
• HappMacDonald批评Seed7中继承自Pascal的缩写习惯（如"func", "proc", "writeln"），主张使用完整的英文单词，认为缩写是编码中的不良习惯。同时提到人工智能可以帮助找到更简洁的表达方式。
• codr7认为Seed7的语法过于复杂，试图通过填充词使其更像英语是编程语言设计中的死胡同。
• pepoluan建议用"99 Bottles of Beer"替代"Hello World"作为强制示例程序。
• msie不喜欢Seed7中将函数声明后赋值给变量的语法，质疑其是否真的优雅。

补充讨论：
• johnisgood简单表示对Seed7感兴趣，但没有深入评论。
• 评论中还提到了过去关于Seed7的讨论链接，表明该语言在较长时间内并未获得广泛关注（例如2009年和2015年的讨论只有少量评论）。

争议焦点：
• Seed7的语法设计，尤其是其类英语语法和缩写使用，引发了关于可读性和编码习惯的争议。HappMacDonald和codr7对语言的语法复杂性和缩写持负面看法，而helix278则欣赏其设计决策。
• msie对函数声明和赋值方式的质疑反映了一部分开发者对Seed7语法风格的怀疑。

Welcome to the Seed7 Homepage
Seed7 is a general purpose programming language designed by Thomas Mertes.
It is a higher level language compared to Ada, C/C++ and Java.
The Seed7
interpreter
and the
example programs
are open-source software.
There is also an open-source Seed7
compiler
. The compiler translates Seed7
programs to C programs which are subsequently compiled to machine code.
In Seed7 new statements and operators can be declared easily.
Functions with type results and type parameters are more elegant
than a template or generics concept.
Object orientation is used where it brings advantages and
not in places where other solutions are more obvious.
Seed7 contains several concepts from Pascal, Ada, C, C++ and Java.
Features of Seed7
As an
extensible programming language
it supports user defined
statements
and
operators
.
Types are first class objects (
Templates and generics
can be defined easily without special syntax).
Predefined constructs like arrays or
for-loops
are defined in libraries.
Object orientation
supports interfaces and
multiple dispatch
.
Static type checking
and the absence of
automatic casts
help to find errors at compile-time.
There is an
automatic memory management
that works without a garbage collection
process.
Exception handling
and
source code debugging
are supported.
If an integer computation
overflows
the exception
OVERFLOW_ERROR
is raised.
Numbers which have unlimited size are provided with the types
bigInteger
and
bigRational
.
Functions, operators and statements can be
overloaded
.
There are various
predefined types
like
array
,
hash
,
set
,
struct
,
color
,
time
,
duration
, etc.
Seed7 programs are
source code portable
without any need to change the code.
Seed7 provides a
database independent API
, which can
connect to MySQL, MariaDB, SQLLite, PostgreSQL, Oracle, ODBC, Firebird, Interbase,
Db2, Informix and SQL Server databases.
Seed7 runs under Linux, various Unix versions and Windows.
The interpreter and the example programs use the GPL
license, while the runtime library uses the LGPL license.
44774027.article_summary: Seed7是一种由Thomas Mertes设计的高级编程语言，具备开源解释器和编译器，编译器将Seed7程序转换为C程序并编译为机器码。Seed7支持用户自定义语句和操作符，具有无特殊语法即可定义模板和泛型的能力。它采用静态类型检查，无自动类型转换，提升编译时错误检测能力。Seed7具备自动内存管理，无需垃圾回收，支持异常处理和源码调试。它提供大整数和大有理数类型，支持函数、操作符和语句的重载。预定义多种数据类型和数据库独立API，可连接多种数据库。Seed7代码具有良好的可移植性，适用于Linux、Unix和Windows系统。解释器和示例程序使用GPL许可，运行库使用LGPL许可。

主要讨论点：Seed7编程语言的特性、设计选择及社区反馈

不同观点：
• OtomotO认为Seed7的创造者非常友善且聪明，语言设计精巧，但Seed7过于小众，令人感到遗憾。
• helix278作为一个函数式编程和抽象数据类型（ADT）的爱好者，赞赏Seed7的内存管理和灵活的语法，认为其设计决策优于C++。具体优点包括：1) 限制内存分配和引用，减少内存管理问题；2) 语法灵活，支持更高层次的抽象。
• HappMacDonald批评Seed7中继承自Pascal的缩写习惯（如"func", "proc", "writeln"），主张使用完整的英文单词，认为缩写是编码中的不良习惯。同时提到人工智能可以帮助找到更简洁的表达方式。

data.title: A Real PowerBook: The Macintosh Application Environment on a Pa-RISC Laptop
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了1997年时，RDI公司推出的一款基于PA-RISC架构的PrecisionBook笔记本电脑，与当时苹果和摩托罗拉主导的PowerPC架构的PowerBook形成对比。尽管Motorola 68000系列的后续通常被认为是PowerPC，但Commodore曾计划使用PA-RISC架构开发Amiga后续产品。RDI的PrecisionBook配备160MHz PA-7300LC处理器，拥有更高的分辨率、更大的内存和硬盘容量，支持HP-UX和Mac 68K软件，价格高达12,000美元。文章还回顾了RDI公司历史，其最初生产SPARC架构笔记本，后因市场变化转向PA-RISC。尽管PrecisionBook性能强劲，但因价格高昂和市场竞争，未能广泛普及。文章最后探讨了如果PowerBook基于PA-RISC，是否会成为一种更具性价比的选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple的MAE（Macintosh Application Environment）及其相关的技术背景和历史

不同观点：
• ethan_smith认为MAE是苹果在Unix工作站上运行Mac OS的一次有趣尝试。它通过创建一个兼容层，将Mac Toolbox调用转换为X11，使得Unix用户无需Apple硬件就能运行Mac软件。这个观点强调了MAE的技术实现和目的。

• esafak则回忆起HP的PA-RISC架构，提到自己年轻时曾为获取相关资料而向HP发传真的经历，表达了对过去HP作为强有力竞争者时代的怀念。这个观点带有个人怀旧情感，并涉及到PA-RISC与讨论主题的技术关联。

• Telemakhos的评论带有调侃性质，提到RISC Mac让他联想到电影《Mission Impossible》，暗示在技术实现或概念上的困难和复杂性。这个观点并没有深入技术细节，而是通过文化联想表达了对技术挑战的看法。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及了不同技术的历史背景，包括MAE的技术细节和PA-RISC的历史地位。
• 讨论中还反映了对过去技术黄金时代的怀念，以及对复杂技术实现的幽默看待。
• 争议的焦点并不明显，但不同评论者关注的角度不同：有人关注技术实现，有人关注历史背景，还有人通过文化联想表达看法。

44774567.article_content:
I like the Power ISA very much, but there's nothing architecturally obvious to say that the next natural step from the Motorola 68000 family must be to PowerPC. For example, the Palm OS
moved from the DragonBall to ARM
, and it's not necessarily a well-known fact that the successor to Commodore's 68K Amigas was intended to be based on PA-RISC, Hewlett-Packard's "Precision Architecture" processor family. (That was
the Hombre chipset
, and
prototype chips existed
prior to Commodore's demise in 1994, though controversy swirled regarding backwards compatibility.) Sure, Apple and Motorola were two-thirds of the AIM alliance, and there were several PowerPC PowerBooks available when the fall of 1997 rolled around. But what if the next PowerBooks had been based on PA-RISC instead?
Well, no need to strain yourself imagining it. Here's nearly as close as you're gonna get.
In October 1997 you could have bought a PowerBook 3400c running up to a 240MHz PowerPC 603e for $6500 [about $13,000 in 2025 dollars], which was briefly billed as the world's fastest laptop, or you could have bought this monster new to the market, the RDI PrecisionBook running up to a 160MHz (later 180MHz) PA-7300LC starting at $12,000 [$24,000]. Both provided onboard Ethernet, SCSI and CardBus PCMCIA slots. On the other hand, while the 3400c had an internal media bay for either a floppy or CD-ROM, both external options on the PrecisionBook, the PrecisionBook gave you a 1024x768 LCD (versus 800x600 on the 3400c), a bigger keyboard, at least two 2.5" hard disk bays and up to 512MB of RAM (versus 144MB) — and HP-UX.
And, through the magic of Apple's official Macintosh Application Environment, you could do anything on it an HP PA-RISC workstation could do and run 68K Mac software on it at the same time. Look at the photograph and see: on our 160MHz unit we've got HP-UX 11.00 CDE running simultaneously with a full Macintosh System 7.5.3 desktop. Yes, only a real Power Mac could run PowerPC software back then, but 68K software was still plentiful and functional. Might this have been a viable option to have your expensive cake and eat it too? We'll find out and run some real apps on it (including
that
game we must all try running), analyze its performance and technical underpinnings, and uncover an unusual artifact of its history hidden in the executable.
(A shout-out to Paul Weissman, the author and maintainer of the incomparable PA-RISC resource
OpenPA.net
, who provided helpful insights for this article.)
In this entry the hardware is at least as unusual as the software we'll be running on it, so let's start with the story of the hardware since it's a bit shorter. Yet another computer manufacturer
near my childhood hometown
, RDI Computer Systems was founded in 1989 as Research, Development and Innovations Incorporated in La Costa, California, a neighbourhood of Carlsbad annexed in 1972 in northern San Diego county.
(It is completely unrelated to earlier Carlsbad company RDI
Video
Systems, short for "Rick Dyer Industries" and the developers of laserdisc games like
Dragon's Lair
and
Space Ace
, who folded in 1985 after their expensive Halcyon home console imploded mid-development from the 1983 video game crash.)
RDI, like several of its contemporaries, was established to capitalize on Sun Microsystems' attempt to commoditize SPARC and open up the market to other OEMs. While most such vendors like
Solbourne Computer
heavily invested in the desktop workstation segment, RDI instead went even smaller, producing what would become the first SPARC laptops in the United States. Basically SPARCstation IPC and IPX systems crammed into boxy off-white portable cases, the BriteLite series weighed a bit over 13 pounds and started at $10,000 [$24,600]. They were lauded for their performance and compatibility but not their battery life, and RDI became an early adopter of Sun's lower-power microSPARC for the sleeker, sexier PowerLites, using a more dramatic jet-black case. An 85MHz microSPARC II PowerLite 85 was the machine that computational physicist Tsutomu Shimomura, then at the San Diego Supercomputer Center, used to track down hacker Kevin Mitnick in 1995.
RDI's initial success enabled its expansion into a bigger 40,000-square foot industrial park facility at 2300 Faraday Avenue, which apparently still exists today. Unfortunately for the company, however, microSPARC hit a performance wall above 125MHz and Sun abandoned further development in 1994, which RDI management took as an indication they needed to diversify. By then the RISC market had started to flourish with many architectures competing for dominance, and RDI decided to throw in with Hewlett-Packard's PA-RISC which had extant portable systems already from Hitachi
and SAIC
. Neither of those systems had ever existed in large numbers (and the SAIC Galaxys only in military applications at that), giving RDI a new market opportunity with a respected architecture that was already mobile-capable. Producing a fin

data.title: Build Your Own Minisforum N5 Inspired Mini NAS
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NAS（网络附加存储）构建的选择、优缺点以及替代方案

不同观点：
• **diggan**：计划在发布几个月后公开Shapr3D设计文件，以便在公开之前解决潜在问题。同时，寻求其他3D打印NAS机箱的灵感。
• **bane**：支持使用便宜的4-bay Mediasonic Proboxes，认为这些设备性价比高，性能稳定，且比一体化NAS系统更具扩展性和持久性。
• **zevon**：使用旧笔记本和随机硬盘作为NAS，赞赏这种便宜且有效的方案。
• **choonway**：认为文中的NAS方案已经过时，推荐更强大且具备更多功能的设备，如Aoostar WTR Max。
• **noelwelsh**：正在考虑构建NAS，发现此文章开启了新的思路，并参考了其他构建方案。
• **rusk**：认为NAS构建不仅在于硬件，软件调试同样重要，最终选择购买一体化NAS以避免软件问题。
• **poemxo**：对文章中Noctua风扇的展示方式表示不满，希望有JBOD版本以配合Mac Mini使用，并对价格表示疑虑。
• **bsder**：对使用打印塑料材料制作NAS机箱表示兴趣，认为主要问题在于成本。
• **pama**：质疑为何需要高性能NAS，认为Raspberry Pi 5可能足够。
• **superkuh**：提出不构建NAS，直接将硬盘安装在常用电脑中，认为这样更具价格、性能和可靠性优势。
• **ggm**：关注m.2到SATA适配器的磁盘IO性能，分享了自己的类似构建方案，使用zimablade和PCI卡。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：NAS构建的必要性和性价比。部分用户（如bane）认为自己构建更具优势，而rusk和superkuh则认为一体化NAS或直接使用电脑更方便。
• **硬件选择**：不同用户推荐了多种硬件方案，从便宜的Mediasonic Proboxes到高性能的Aoostar WTR Max，以及Raspberry Pi 5。
• **软件调试**：rusk强调了NAS软件调试的复杂性，推荐一体化软件解决方案如unRAID。
• **性能与成本**：讨论中多次提到性能与成本的平衡，特别是高性能NAS是否必要以及便宜方案的可行性。

这些观点展示了NAS构建中的多样化选择和个人偏好，以及硬件和软件方面的考虑。

data.title: People still use our old-fashioned Unix login servers
data.author: sugarpimpdorsey
data.article_summary: 本文是博客作者Chris Siebenmann对使用过时浏览器访问其博客或wiki（CSpace）的用户发出的警告。由于2025年初高流量爬虫（包括用于LLM训练的数据爬虫）大量使用旧版浏览器用户代理，特别是Chrome，作者采取了封锁措施。如果用户因这些措施被误挡，且实际上使用的是最新版浏览器，可以联系作者提供所用浏览器的详细信息（如User-Agent字符串）。此外，通过archive.*（如archive.today、archive.ph等）访问的用户也可能被误挡，因为这些网站的爬取行为类似于恶意爬虫。作者建议使用更为规范的archive.org进行存档访问。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：登录服务器（login server）的用途和替代方案

不同观点：
• [rwmj] 认为登录服务器非常实用，特别是在以下场景中：保存Git备份、通过SCP传输文件、上传供同事获取的文件、以及作为永久IRC端点。他还指出，云VM或容器不适合这些用途，因为需要永久存在且用户间共享的系统（通过独立的Unix账户）。

• [teekert] 提到超级计算机如荷兰的Snellius和芬兰的Lumi都是Slurm集群，带有登录节点。特别是对于生物信息学等领域，在一个良好管理的Slurm集群上工作能获得极高的性价比（包括GPU和大型节点）。

• [nickdothutton] 正在建立一个现代的shell主机社区，将其视为高信任度的社交网络利基市场，为志同道合的人提供服务。

• [ValtteriL] 分享了在大学服务器上运行irssi的经历，以及通过X转发远程完成Matlab作业的实例。他提到管理员鼓励用户对进程进行nice操作，但他的密码破解会话总是被终止。

• [jstanley] 对"login server"的定义提出疑问，认为任何可以登录的服务器都可以称为登录服务器。

• [PeterStuer] 提到在远程服务器上运行VScode后端的技术问题，质疑这种用法是否符合共享服务器的初衷，认为可能是由于免费和可用性而被使用。

• [somat] 分享了自己创建的理想社交网络项目，虽然自嘲为“愚蠢”的想法，但从中获得了乐趣。

• [charcircuit] 建议开放其他机器到互联网，并推荐用户将代码上传到GitHub，而不是学校的文件服务器。对于读取邮件和定时任务（cron jobs），他认为需要先了解具体需求再提出替代方案。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：登录服务器的必要性和替代方案。一部分人（如rwmj和teekert）认为登录服务器有不可替代的优势，而其他人（如charcircuit）则提出可能的替代方案。

• 有趣的项目：nickdothutton和somat分享了他们创建社区和社交网络项目的经验和乐趣。

• 实际操作中的问题：ValtteriL提到了在大学服务器上操作时遇到的进程管理和资源限制问题。

You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.

data.article_summary: 文章揭示了北卡罗来纳州许多高分学生未被安排进高级数学课程的问题。研究发现，超过一半有望在高级数学中成功的学生未被安排进这些课程，尤其是一些低收入和少数族裔学生，尽管他们成绩优异。传统上，高级数学课程需要教师推荐，但数据表明许多高分学生并未获得推荐。2009年的一项分析显示，约35,000名初中生本应在8年级学习代数，但未被安排，尽管他们在9年级代数考试中表现优异。文章指出，这种系统性问题浪费了大量学生潜力。一些学校通过取消教师推荐要求，让高分学生进入高级课程，结果证明这些学生能够成功适应高级课程。文章呼吁改革数学课程安排，确保高分学生有机会接受更具挑战性的教育。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国中学数学课程安排的现状及其问题，特别是代数I课程的获取和高级课程的推荐机制。

不同观点：
• rahimnathwani：指出旧金山数学课程安排存在问题，八年级学生很难在学年内获得面对面的代数I课程，尽管该地区每个学生的平均运营支出很高。
• djoldman：认为通过教师推荐来决定学生是否能上高级课程会导致偏见，并提到北卡罗来纳州通过的法律，要求标准化测试高分学生自动进入高级课程，以此解决偏见问题。他还指出人类判断常常出错，暗示自动化可能有帮助。
• recursivecaveat：对将高级数学课程视为稀缺资源感到不满，认为这种做法会导致教育上的不平等，即“有”和“没有”的状况。
• vorgol：质疑如果不掌握代数，如何能学习高级数学，暗示代数是基础。
• zozbot234：认为将代数I视为“高级”数学是美国特有的问题，在欧洲和东亚并不存在，称其为“低期望的软性偏见”。
• chriscrisby：提出是否研究了那些数学好但不感兴趣的学生的情况，质疑是否所有学生都应被推向高级课程。
• thevillagechief：对美国通过行政和家长干预限制学生选择课程的做法感到沮丧，指出大多数国家没有这种高级课程分级制度，认为这是精英阶层维护自身优势的手段。
• anovikov：认为有限的教育资源应优先分配给更有可能在生活中应用这些知识的学生，暗示资源分配应考虑实际需求。
• elric：反驳大规模未能上高级课程就是浪费人类潜力的说法，认为未上代数课程的学生可能在其他课程上表现良好，不认为这是人生失败或浪费潜力的表现。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于高级数学课程的获取和分配机制，特别是在推荐机制中的人类偏见问题，以及是否应将高级课程视为稀缺资源进行分配。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是资源分配的公平性和效率问题，以及不同国家教育制度的对比。
• 对于是否所有学生都应被推向高级课程，存在分歧，部分人认为应尊重学生的兴趣和选择，而不是强制所有人都上高级课程。

More than half of students predicted to succeed in advanced math are denied access to those classes.
Our research firm evaluates federally funded education programs in K-12 schools. In the early to mid-2000s, these grant-funded program evaluations began requiring measurable objectives and pre- and post-data comparisons. During this period, federal grants aimed at getting more low-income and minority students into advanced STEM courses became a common trend.
These program evaluation requirements led to a striking discovery. Tens of thousands of high-scoring students in North Carolina were not enrolled in advanced math courses. When staff working on the grant-funded programs (typically school counselors, school improvement teams, and administrators) discovered they already had hundreds of top-scoring, academically successful students in a single middle or high school who were not in advanced math, they usually wanted to enroll them. More often than not, they were told by their math departments that they couldn't enroll these students because students needed a teacher recommendation.
Educators involved in these grant-funded programs became curious about who was actually enrolled in advanced math and how those students had gained access. They asked us to examine the data to find out, as they had simply assumed that the students with the highest math scores were the ones in advanced math classes. Very few low-income and minority students were enrolled in advanced math, and the school counselors and administrators assumed this was because these students didn't score high on assessments. This incorrect assumption led them to write objectives for their grant-funded programs focused on increasing the number of low-income and minority students who scored high in math, believing there were virtually none. They had also incorrectly assumed that if their grant-funded services resulted in these students scoring higher that they would enroll in advanced math.
Subscribe
When academic achievement and advanced enrollment diverge
In 2009, North Carolina administrators were becoming more aware that enrollment in advanced math classes was not done by academic achievement, largely due to the new trend of federal grants aimed at increasing enrollment of low-income and minority students. The North Carolina Association of School Administrators hired us to work with SAS to investigate how math placement related to math achievement in all school districts in the state.
SAS Institute analyzed academic scores and math course enrollment patterns for all of North Carolina and for each school system.
SAS Institute
is a leading global provider of advanced analytics and statistical software, with over 12,000 employees and more than 80,000 customer sites in 140 countries, making it a major player in enterprise data solutions across industry and academia. Their analysis revealed the extent of these placement gaps. Among 7th graders with strong statistical predictions for success in advanced math, fewer than 50% were actually placed in 8th-grade algebra. At the same time, many students in those advanced classes had lower success predictions than students who were not recommended for the class.
This is not a small problem affecting a few students. This analysis revealed a systematic failure affecting tens of thousands of children across North Carolina alone, wasting human potential on a massive scale. The study done in 2009 showed that about 35,000 North Carolina middle school students were predicted to be successful in 8th-grade algebra but were not enrolled. They went on to take 9th-grade algebra, and more than 25,000 of them scored at the highest level on the 9th-grade algebra end-of-grade test. Yet despite this demonstrated high performance, they remained in the standard track rather than advancing to more rigorous mathematics courses, such as Honors, Advanced Placement, or IB math classes.
1
In some schools that we worked with, either evaluating their grants or helping them with their school improvement plans, principals overrode the typical placement requirement of teacher recommendations and enrolled all high-scoring students into the advanced math track. If we were working on the evaluation of a grant-funded program we would follow the students’ progress over several years. Nearly all students who were moved to the advanced math track based on their academic scores were successful in earning As or Bs in the courses and remained on the advanced track. data.title: Flourishing chemosynthetic life at the greatest depths of hadal trenches
data.author: smartmic
data.article_summary: 文章报道了在库里尔-堪察加海沟和阿留申海沟深处发现的大规模化学合成生命群落。这些群落位于5,800米至9,533米深度，由富含氢硫化物和甲烷的流体维持，主要包括多毛类和双壳类生物。这些流体通过海沟中的地质断层输送，甲烷由沉积有机物经微生物生成。这一发现挑战了现有关于极端环境下生命和深海碳循环的理论，表明化学合成群落可能在其他超深海沟中也广泛存在。此前，类似群落的记录非常稀少，尤其是深度超过6,000米的海沟中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：视频内容引发的对深海生物和地球灾难后生命恢复的讨论

不同观点：
• [乐观观点] narrator认为，如果有巨型陨石撞击地球，深海中的生物可能成为地球生命恢复的希望。这种观点基于深海生物对极端环境的适应能力，尤其是在深海的极端压力和黑暗环境下，它们可能具备更强的生存韧性。

• [知识补充观点] Mistletoe提供了关于“hadal”这个词的定义，指出它指的是海深约20,000英尺（6,000米）以下的区域。这补充了关于深海生物生存环境的背景知识，帮助其他人理解深海生物可能在极端条件下存活的依据。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中隐含了对深海生态系统的关注，尤其是它们在面对全球性灾难时的潜在生存优势。虽然没有明确提出争议，但narrator的乐观态度与现实中科学界对深海生物了解的有限性之间可能存在讨论空间。

• 另一个值得注意的点是，评论没有直接涉及如何具体利用深海生物来“重启”地球生命，这可能引发进一步的科学探讨和技术可行性讨论。

Flourishing chemosynthetic life at the greatest depths of hadal trenches
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Carbon cycle
Ecosystem ecology
Marine biology
Abstract
Hadal trenches, some of the Earth’s least explored and understood environments, have long been proposed to harbour chemosynthesis-based communities
1
,
2
. Despite increasing attention, actual documentation of such communities has been exceptionally rare
3
,
4
. Here we report the discovery of the deepest and the most extensive chemosynthesis-based communities known to exist on Earth during an expedition to the Kuril–Kamchatka Trench and the western Aleutian Trench using the manned submersible
Fendouzhe
. The communities dominated by siboglinid Polychaeta and Bivalvia span a distance of 2,500 km at depths from 5,800 m to 9,533 m. These communities are sustained by hydrogen sulfide-rich and methane-rich fluids that are transported along faults traversing deep sediment layers in trenches, where methane is produced microbially from deposited organic matter, as indicated by isotopic analysis. Given geological similarities with other hadal trenches, such chemosynthesis-based communities might be more widespread than previously anticipated. These findings challenge current models of life at extreme limits and carbon cycling in the deep ocean.

Chemosynthesis-based communities represent a remarkable example of life’s ability to adapt and thrive in some of the most extreme conditions on Earth
5
,
6
,
7
,
8
. Since the initial discovery of these communities at hydrothermal vents
9
, the detection of chemosynthesis-based communities at cold seeps, supporting highly diverse and abundant chemosymbiotic biota
1
,
3
,
4
,
5
,
6
,
7
,
8
, has increased and expanded our understanding of deep-sea ecological systems and the biogeochemical processes that underpin them. The communities, typically dominated by Bivalvia and Siboglinidae, and sustained by microbial chemosynthesis, are confined to areas where fluids rich in hydrogen sulfide and/or methane are released through geological fractures
6
,
7
.
Despite being found on passive and active margins across a wide range of ocean depths
5
,
6
,
7
,
8
, cold-seep communities have remained largely unexplored in hadal trenches with depths exceeding 6,000 m. Only two small seep communities at hadal depths have been discovered by submersible and remotely operated vehicle, one dominated by vesicomyid clams at nearly 6,437 m depth and another dominated by thyasirid clams at 7,326–7,434 m in the Japan Trench
3
,
4
,
10
. In addition, probable chemosynthetic mats have been observed at a depth of 10,677 m at the bottom of the Mariana Trench
11
; however, they are not associated with any seep animal communities. The biogeographical distribution of chemosynthesis-based communities in the deepest parts of the world’s oceans, their potential roles in shaping the deep-sea ecosystem and the mechanisms behind the formation of methane seeps at such great depths remain elusive.
The Kuril–Kamchatka Trench and the Aleutian Trench are formed by the tectonic interactions between the Pacific Plate and the North American Plate, and meet at the Kamchatka Aleutian Transition connection
12
. This area is geologically highly active with many seismically and volcanically active sites. The Kuril–Kamchatka Trench is formed by the northwestward subduction of the Pacific Plate beneath the Okhotsk Plate and extends around 2,100 km from Hokkaido in the south to Kamchatka Peninsula in the north
13
. The maximum depth of the trench bottom reaches 9,578 m, based on our submersible conductivity–temperature–depth data. Previous research conducted by expeditions aboard research vessel (RV)
Vityaz
and RV
Sonne
in the Kuril–Kamchatka Trench shows that the trench is characterized by predominantly heterotrophic benthic fauna
14
,
15
. However, some specimens of chemosymbiotrophic taxa
15
,
16
, in particular frenulate siboglinids, were also recovered using a trawl, indicating that methane seeps may exist on the trench bottom. The Aleutian Trench is about 2,900 km long, extends from the Alaska and Kenai peninsulas in North America to Kamchatka
13
and marks a boundary where the Pacific Plate has been subducting northwestwards beneath the Bering Sea Plate. Both trenches underlie a highly productive boreal region of the North Pacific Ocean and are characterized by distinct spring blooms and high annual primary production
17
.

data.title: If You're Remote, Ramble
data.author: lawgimenez
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种适用于2-10人远程团队的沟通技巧，即在团队聊天应用中为每个成员创建一个个人“漫谈”频道。这些频道允许成员分享想法、项目相关点子、博客文章感想、用户反馈、假设性建议、旅行或爱好照片，以及自我思考问题等，类似于个人日记或微型博客。每个频道以成员名字命名，只有该成员能发布主帖，其他人可在线程中回复。所有漫谈频道应归入聊天列表底部的“漫谈”板块，默认静音，不要求每个人都阅读。这种方法在Obsidian团队中实验两年，效果显著，成为无会议情况下保持联系和激发创意的一种方式，有助于减少干扰并促进深度工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：远程工作中的闲聊（rambling）或饮水机式闲谈（water cooler talk）的价值及其在不同团队规模中的可行性。

不同观点：
• [支持观点] rablackburn 认为远程工作中的闲逛或漫步（如早晨1小时的徒步作为“通勤”）有助于区分家庭和工作的界限，同时提供有氧运动和思考时间，非常有价值。bsenftner 也支持通过开放语音频道来创建“共享虚拟空间”，以促进团队的自然交流和社交互动。

• [规模限制] OJFord 和 senko 指出，虽然小团队（2-10人）的闲聊渠道可能有效，但在大型组织中难以扩展，可能导致信息过载。senko 进一步提到，一个通用的非工作相关聊天频道比多个需要跟踪的频道更好。

• [实施挑战] 9dev 和 esperent 认为，新增的聊天频道可能会增加沟通负担，导致员工必须扫描更多信息以保持表面上的参与感。dakiol 提到，这类频道可能演变为对公司或管理层的抱怨场所，容易引发负面情绪。

• [个人化与公共性] makeitdouble 质疑个人化频道的必要性，认为饮水机式闲谈的本质是非个人的。gwbas1c 分享了创建“饮水机”频道的经验，以将闲聊与主要工作频道分开，便于管理。

• [其他应用] marginalia_nu 和 bobek 提到，记录想法和半成品思考在独自工作或深度工作时也非常有用，可以捕捉到转瞬即逝的灵感。

补充讨论：
• [文化差异] skhameneh 强调，健康的远程优先公司与传统以办公室为中心的公司在社交互动上的不同，认为这类闲谈是远程工作文化的一部分。

• [个人经验] codesnik 分享了尝试在远程公司中创建或复活饮水机式聊天频道的经验，指出某些团队可能不需要或选择私下交流，而非使用公共频道。

总体而言，讨论围绕远程工作环境中闲聊或闲谈的价值、其实施方式及潜在挑战展开，涉及规模适应性、团队文化及个人需求等多个方面。

44775563.article_content:
If you're remote, ramble
July 31, 2025
·
1 minute read
A tip for remote teams of 2-10 people. Create a personal “ramblings” channel for each teammate in your team’s chat app of choice.
Ramblings channels let everyone share what’s on their mind without cluttering group channels. Think of them as personal journals or microblogs inside your team’s chat app, a lightweight way to add ambient social cohesion.
People typically post short updates 1-3 times per week. Common topics include:
ideas related to current projects
musings about blog posts, articles, user feedback
“what if” suggestions
photos from recent trips or hobbies
rubber ducking a problem
Each ramblings channel should be named after the team member, and only that person can post top-level messages. Others can reply in threads, but not start new ones.
All the ramblings channels should be in a
Ramblings
section at the bottom of the channel list. They should be muted by default, with no expectation that anyone else will read them.
We started experimenting with ramblings at
Obsidian
two years ago, and they’ve been surprisingly sticky. We have no scheduled meetings, so ramblings are our equivalent of water cooler talk. We want as much deep focus time as possible, so ramblings help us stay connected while minimizing interruptions.
Because they are so free and loose, some of our best ideas emerge from ramblings. They’re often the source of feature ideas, small prototypes, and creative solutions to long-standing problems.
About once a year, we do a week-long in-person meetup. Ramblings have been one successful way we keep the human connection going throughout the rest of the year.

data.title: 2,500-year-old Siberian 'ice mummy' had intricate tattoos, imaging reveals
data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 高分辨率影像揭示了一具2500年前的西伯利亚“冰尸”身上的复杂纹身。这具女性木乃伊属于游牧民族帕兹里克人，其纹身包括豹、鹿、公鸡以及狮身鹰首兽等神话生物，展示了古代战士文化的艺术风格。通过与纹身艺术家的合作，研究人员发现这些纹身技艺精湛，可能使用了多点和单点工具以及植物烧成的颜料。纹身质量在两只手臂上有所不同，可能由不同人完成或因失误导致。研究还表明，纹身可能在生前具有重要意义，而在死后并不重要。这些发现发表在《古代》期刊上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：古代纹身的艺术价值、历史背景及其在社会中的意义

不同观点：
• **纹身的艺术性与现代纹身师的比较**：
  - [romanhn] 认为这些木乃伊上的纹身具有很高的艺术性，并对研究者通过历史方法在自己身上重现古代纹身设计表示惊讶。
  - [dclowd9901] 反驳文章中关于现代纹身师难以复制古代纹身的观点，认为现代优秀纹身师在技术和艺术性上都非常出色。

• **纹身的历史和文化背景**：
  - [topspin] 强调这些纹身展示了比中世纪绘画更好的透视、动作和比例表达，认为这是真正的艺术。
  - [VTimofeenko] 分享了其祖父在苏联时期听到的关于西伯利亚北部面部纹身作为宗教和地位象征的故事，并指出该传统在不同地区之间的传播。
  - [casenmgreen] 认为虽然2500年前的纹身艺术可能存在，但与同时期的希腊文明相比，西伯利亚地区的人民在其他方面（如商业、建筑等）并不发达。

• **纹身的意义和社会地位**：
  - [koevet] 表示对Pazyryk木乃伊纹身风格有强烈情感共鸣，并决定在自己的身体上纹上相似的动物图案。
  - [Theodores] 从社会学角度分析纹身在现代和古代社会中的流行及其意义，认为纹身文化表明了社会的富裕程度和职业分工，同时指出纹身在个体层面上反映的童年创伤和社会层面的复杂性。

补充讨论：
• **纹身的真实性与保存方法**：
  - [treis] 质疑这些是否为真正的纹身，还是死后在皮肤上绘制的图案。
  
• **纹身图案的象征意义**：
  - [lupusreal] 指出纹身中的狮鹫图案具有重要意义，并引用希腊和罗马文献中的相关描述来支持这一观点。

• **技术与健康问题**：
  - [userbinator] 关心这些纹身图像是否经过后期处理，尤其是是否经过AI增强。
  - [giardini] 开玩笑地认为这些古人可能死于肝炎，暗示古代纹身过程中的卫生问题。

• **伦理与考古价值**：
  - [wileydragonfly] 质疑从2500年前的尸体中学到有价值的东西是否值得将其暴露在外，反映了对考古伦理的关注。

争议焦点：
• 现代纹身师是否能复制古代纹身设计的技巧和艺术性。
• 古代纹身在现代视角下的文化价值和社会意义。
• 考古发现中的伦理问题，尤其是对尸体处理的合理性。

44745441.article_content:
2,500-year-old Siberian 'ice mummy' had intricate tattoos, imaging reveals
4 days ago
Share
Save
Georgina Rannard
Science correspondent
Share
Save
G Caspari and M Vavulin
Scans of the ice mummy's skin revealed details of animals and birds on her arms and hands
High-resolution imaging of tattoos found on a 2,500 year old Siberian "ice mummy" have revealed decorations that a modern tattooist would find challenging to produce, according to researchers.
The intricate tattoos of leopards, a stag, a rooster, and a mythical half-lion and half-eagle creature on the woman's body shed light on an ancient warrior culture.
Archaeologists worked with a tattooist, who reproduces ancient skin decorations on his own body, to understand how exactly they were made.
The tattooed woman, aged about 50, was from the nomadic horse-riding Pazyryk people who lived on the vast steppe between China and Europe.
Daniel Riday
An illustration of the tattoo on the woman's right forearm revealed in new scans
The scans revealed "intricate crisp and uniform" tattooing that could not be seen with the naked eye.
"The insights really drive home to me the point of how sophisticated these people were," lead author Dr Gino Caspari from the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology and the University of Bern, told BBC News.
It is difficult to uncover detailed information about ancient social and cultural practices because most evidence is destroyed over time. It is even harder to get up close to the details of one person's life.
The Pazyryk "ice mummies" were found inside ice tombs in the Altai mountains in Siberia in the 19th century, but it has been difficult to see the tattoos.
Daniel Riday
An illustration of the tattoo on the woman's left forearm revealed in new scans
Now using near-infrared digital photography in the Hermitage Museum in St Petersburg, Russia experts have created high resolution scans of the decorations for the first time.
"This made me feel like we were much closer to seeing the people behind the art, how they worked and learned. The images came alive," Dr Caspari said.
On her right forearm, the Pazyryk woman had an image of leopards around the head of a deer.
Getty Images
The Pazyryk were a nomadic group that lived in the Altai mountains
On the left arm, the mythical griffin creature with the body of a lion and the head and wings of an eagle appears to be fighting with a stag.
"Twisted hind bodies and really intense battle scenes of wild animals are typical of the culture," Dr Caspari said.
But the woman also had a rooster on her thumb, showing "an intriguing style with a certain uniqueness," says Dr Caspari.
The team worked with researcher Daniel Riday who reproduces ancient tattoo designs on his body using historical methods.
Daniel Riday
Daniel Riday uses pre-electric methods to tattoo ancient decorations on his skin
A 'solid commitment'
His insights on the scans led them to conclude that the quality of the work differed between the two arms, suggesting that a different person made the tattoos or that mistakes were made.
"If I was guessing, it was probably four and half hours for the lower half of the right arm, and another five hours for the upper part," he says.
"That's a solid commitment from the person. Imagine sitting on the ground in the steppe where there's wind blowing all that time," he suggests.
"It would need to be performed by a person who knows health and safety, who knows the risks of what happens when the skin is punctured," he adds.
High-resolution scans and images of the woman's skin give insights into the tattoo method
By analysing the marks in the woman's skin, the team believe that the tattoos were probably stencilled onto the skin before being tattooed.
They think a needle-like tool with small multiple points probably made from animal horn or bone was used, as well as a single point needle. The pigment was likely made from burnt plant material or soot.
Dr Caspari, who does not have tattoos himself, says the work sheds light on an ancient practice that is very important for a lot of people around the world today.
Daniel Riday
An illustration of the tattoo on the woman's thumb and fingers
"And back in the day it was already a really professional practice where people put a lot of time and effort and practice into creating these images and they're extremely sophisticated," he adds.
Some of the tattoos appear to have been cut or damaged when the body was prepared for burial.
"It suggests that tattoos were really something for the living with meaning during life, but that they actually didn't really play much of a role in the afterlife," explains Dr Caspari.
The findings are published in the journal Antiquity.
M Vavulin
Several ice mummies were found in the Altai mountains and they are currently kept at the Hermitage Museum in Russia

• brabel：认为长时间的假期不必要，自己更倾向于少休假并将部分假期积累下来，同时表示即便休假也会因为无聊而继续工作。这种观点强调个人对休假的不同需求，以及工作本身带来的满足感。

data.author: adriencaccia
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在持续集成（CI）环境中设置性能门限以防止重大性能回退的挑战，尤其是在云托管的CI运行器中进行性能测量时，由于虚拟化层的干扰导致的噪声问题。文章指出，性能回退如果未及时发现，修复成本会更高，因此在开发阶段捕捉问题至关重要。作者通过在GitHub Actions托管运行器上运行多种基准测试套件，计算其变异系数（Coefficient of Variation, CV），发现变异系数为2.66%。这意味着如果设置2%的性能门限，误报概率高达45%。为将误报率控制在1%，性能门限需设为7%，但这会导致较小的性能回退无法被检测到。最终，文章强调在云CI环境中进行有效性能测试的难度，并建议寻找更稳定的基准测试方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何有效进行性能测试和避免假正率（false positive rate）过高的问题，特别是在使用GitHub Actions等非确定性环境下的性能测试。

不同观点：
• farkin88：认为GitHub Actions的性能测试受随机性影响较大（例如时间波动导致的高假正率），建议使用确定性的裸机运行器（bare-metal runners）来执行测试，以提高测试的可信度。他提到GitHub Actions的变异系数（CV）为2.66%，导致约45%的假正率，使得开发者难以信任这些检查结果。

• krona：同意farkin88关于假正率的观点，但补充强调，当开发者编写一整套基准测试时，即使单个测试的假正率较低，整套测试仍可能产生较高的总体假正率（例如10%）。这使得问题更加复杂，尤其是在向没有统计背景的开发者或QA解释时。

• atombender：赞赏使用变异系数（CoV）来检测不稳定性，但分享了自己的经验，认为CoV在某些情况下（例如在分析实际请求流量时）并不总是可靠。他提到在进行性能分析时，尝试通过相关性分析来识别问题根源，但由于不同工作负载的不可预测性，问题往往难以隔离。

• IshKebab：提出使用指令计数（instruction counts）作为通过/失败的标准，认为这样更加确定和可靠。同时认为运行时间（wall time）可以作为参考信息，但不应作为主要的判定依据。

补充讨论：
• 假正率的计算和影响是讨论的核心，尤其是当多个测试一起运行时，假正率可能被放大。
• 不同环境（如GitHub Actions与裸机运行器）对测试结果的影响也是争议的焦点，部分参与者认为确定性环境更可靠。
• 除了假正率，如何有效分析和隔离性能问题（如通过相关性分析或使用不同统计技术）也被提及，显示出对更多可靠分析方法的需求。

Creating a performance gate in a CI environment, preventing significant
performance regressions from being deployed has been a long-standing goal of
dozens of software teams. But measuring in hosted CI runners is a particularly
challenging task, mostly because of noisy neighbors leaking through
virtualization layers.
Still, it's worth the effort. Performance regressions are harder to catch and
more expensive to fix the longer they go unnoticed. Mostly because:
Catching issues in production is too late: Once it's deployed, the damage
(slowdown, cost, UX impact) is already done.
Feedback stays close to the code: Catching regressions during development
reduces costly context switching and rework.

Each run is executed on a different machine, simulating real CI conditions.

We stay close to real-world CI variability (one machine per run),
But still benefit from statistical robustness within each run (via repeated

data.author: p-sharpe

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI personas和模拟焦点小组技术在产品测试和用户反馈收集中的应用，及其潜在的伦理问题、准确性、实用性和市场定位。

不同观点：
• [milchek] 对AI personas在焦点小组中的应用表示担忧，特别是其在地方政府决策中的潜在滥用。他认为LLMs无法真实反映人类的复杂性和实际生活经验，过度依赖这些技术可能会导致对人类反馈的误解。
• [rollinDyno] 对该技术的准确性表示怀疑，尤其是与行业标准专用模型相比的预测能力。他质疑该技术是否在所有情况下都能保证最高的准确性。
• [VikRubenfeld] 对该工具的用户界面和体验表示赞赏，但提出关于减少假阳性结果的需求，尤其是在市场研究中的应用。
• [chatmasta] 讨论了产品的目标买家和核心功能定位问题，建议明确产品方向并聚焦于特定用例，以避免功能泛化。他还提出与现有数据提供商合作的建议。
• [jwally] 作为一个初学者，对能够快速、廉价地进行实验表示赞赏，对AI/LLM技术持乐观态度，即使其与现实世界的映射不完全一致。
• [lbrito] 对该工具在LinkedIn帖子反应预测中的准确性表示认可，并期待未来的优化版本。
• [whymsicalburito] 关注AI personas在地理区域和人口统计学上的覆盖能力，质疑是否存在无法模拟的群体。
• [arkokoley] 分享了相关研究论文，讨论了多智能体模拟的长期稳定性和准确性问题，建议可能的技术合作。
• [impostervt] 使用AI创建客户头像来设计产品，但对从"AI生成客户头像"到"模拟真实人"的转变表示兴趣，希望增加客户头像的深度。
• [kevdoran] 赞赏产品的UX设计，并分享了相关研究论文以供参考。
• [digitcatphd] 通过实验发现LLM结果与真实世界数据的差异，认为当前技术在多样性和真实性上仍有不足。
• [StarterPro] 对该技术是否替代了实际的田野研究表示怀疑，认为如果反馈不是来自真实的买家，那么该技术的价值有限。
• [lonelyasacloud] 担心该技术的滥用潜力，特别是用于销售不健康产品或政治宣传，质疑技术进步的伦理影响。
• [jddj] 对用户界面的技术细节提出具体改进建议。
• [lucasverra] 对该工具在LinkedIn策略中的应用表示兴趣，并寻求更多支持和详细信息。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：AI personas是否能够真实反映人类反馈，以及该技术在实际应用中的伦理问题和潜在滥用风险。
• 技术准确性和实用性：多位讨论者关注该技术在不同场景下的准确性和与实际数据的对比，特别是与行业标准模型和真实世界反馈的差异。
• 市场定位和功能聚焦：有建议提出需要明确产品核心功能和目标买家，以避免功能泛化并提高市场适应性。
• 合作和扩展：建议与现有数据提供商或技术平台合作，以增强产品的数据丰富性和市场覆盖。

• [jddj] 对用户界面的技术细节提出具体改进建议。
• [lucasverra] 对该工具在LinkedIn策略中的应用表示兴趣，并寻求更多支持和详细信息。

• 争议焦点：AI personas是否能够真实反映人类反馈，以及该技术在实际应用中的伦理问题和潜在滥用风险。

data.title: Native Sparse Attention
data.author: CalmStorm
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为Natively Sparse Attention（NSA）的新型稀疏注意力机制，旨在提高长上下文建模的效率。NSA结合了算法创新和硬件优化，通过动态层次稀疏策略，兼顾全局上下文感知和局部精度。其两大核心创新包括：平衡算术强度的算法设计和现代硬件优化的实现，显著提升了计算速度；支持端到端训练，减少预训练计算量的同时不牺牲模型性能。实验表明，NSA在长上下文任务和指令推理等基准测试中表现优于传统的全注意力模型，并在处理64k长度序列时实现了显著的速度提升。

Abstract
Long-context modeling is crucial for next-generation language models, yet the high computational cost of standard attention mechanisms poses significant computational challenges. Sparse attention offers a promising direction for improving efficiency while maintaining model capabilities. We present NSA, a Natively trained Sparse Attention mechanism that integrates algorithmic innovations with hardware-aligned optimizations to achieve efficient long-context modeling. NSA employs a dynamic hierarchical sparse strategy, combining coarse-grained token compression with fine-grained token selection to preserve both global context awareness and local precision. Our approach advances sparse attention design with two key innovations: (1) We achieve substantial speedups through arithmetic intensity-balanced algorithm design, with implementation optimizations for modern hardware. (2) We enable end-to-end training, reducing pretraining computation without sacrificing model performance. As shown in Figure 1, experiments show the model pretrained with NSA maintains or exceeds Full Attention models across general benchmarks, long-context tasks, and instruction-based reasoning. Meanwhile, NSA achieves substantial speedups over Full Attention on 64k-length sequences across decoding, forward propagation, and backward propagation, validating its efficiency throughout the model lifecycle.

data.title: Researchers map where solar energy delivers the biggest climate payoff
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 研究人员利用先进的计算模型，分析了美国各地区太阳能对减少二氧化碳排放的即时和延迟效益。研究发现，美国若增加15%的太阳能发电量，每年可减少854万吨二氧化碳排放。然而，不同地区的太阳能投资回报差异显著。加州、佛罗里达、中大西洋地区、德州和西南部地区能获得较大减排效果，而在新英格兰、美国中部和田纳西等地效果不明显。研究还揭示了太阳能采用对邻近地区的溢出效应，例如加州增加15%的太阳能容量，还能减少西北和西南地区的每日二氧化碳排放。该研究为政策制定者和投资者提供了有针对性的太阳能投资指南，以实现最大减排效益。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于太阳能发电对减少二氧化碳排放的效果及相关研究的讨论

不同观点：
• [正面支持] **sabakhoj** 和 **liquidise** 对研究结果表示积极支持，认为太阳能发电的增加显著推动了美国实现气候目标，并分享了研究链接和图表，帮助进一步了解研究细节。

• [地区性讨论] **pards** 引用了研究中的具体发现，指出不同地区（如加利福尼亚、佛罗里达、中西部等）的太阳能发电对减少二氧化碳排放的影响不同，强调了地区差异性。

• [扩展讨论] **smadge** 认为加利福尼亚在环境和气候行动方面有机会成为北美的典范，但同时指出加州在项目推进上是自己最大的阻碍，提出了太阳能之外的其他绿色项目（如高速铁路和公共交通电气化）。

• [技术贡献] **rdtsc** 提供了与绿色能源优化相关的GitHub项目链接，为有兴趣进一步研究或处理数据的人提供了技术支持。

• [批评与质疑] **m0llusk** 通过提及德国露台太阳能的普及，暗示这种基于数据的预测可能无法完全捕捉技术和社会趋势，质疑研究预测的全面性。

• [全面批评] **m101** 对研究的整体思路提出批评，认为仅仅关注二氧化碳排放和太阳能是不够全面的，主张要从更广泛的角度看待所有发电技术，并认为太阳能并非解决气候变化的核心方案，甚至可能是一种“干扰”。

补充讨论：
• [对研究内容的期望] **sophia01** 和 **metonymy** 对文章中提到的“地图”感到困惑或失望，因为他们期待看到实际的地图展示，但文章似乎没有提供。

• [无关评论] **lorenzohess** 提到了一个与讨论主题无关的内容（"On Mercury"），并未对研究或观点做出实际贡献。

• [研究资助背景] **searine** 指出了研究的资助来源，强调该研究得到了美国纳税人资助的多个拨款以及哈佛大学的机构支持，可能意在强调研究的权威性或透明度。

争议焦点：
• 研究是否全面：部分评论（如 **m0llusk** 和 **m101**）质疑研究的预测能力及其对整体环境问题的适用性，认为太阳能只是其中一个方面，而非唯一解决方案。
• 地区差异：不同地区太阳能发电的效果差异显著，这一发现引发了对政策制定和能源规划的进一步思考（**pards** 的评论）。

Researchers Map Where Solar Energy Delivers the Biggest Climate Payoff
Adobe Stock

patti.zielinski@rutgers.edu

Using advanced computational modeling, a Rutgers professor, in collaboration with researchers from the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health and Stony Brook University, reveal both the immediate and delayed climate benefits of solar power
Increasing solar power generation in the United States by 15% could lead to an annual reduction of 8.54 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions, according to researchers at Rutgers, the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health and Stony Brook University.
The
study
, published in
Science Advances
, found that the climate benefits of solar power differ markedly throughout U.S. regions, pinpointing where clean energy investments return the greatest climate dividends.
In 2023, 60% of
U.S. electricity generation
relied on fossil fuels, while 3.9% came from solar, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Because fossil fuel-generated electricity is a
leading source of carbon dioxide
, or CO2, and harmful air pollutants such as fine particulate matter, expanding solar could not only mitigate CO2 but help
reduce illness, hospitalizations and premature deaths
linked to air pollution exposure.
From a computer science perspective, this study demonstrates the power of harnessing large-scale, high-resolution energy data to generate actionable insights.
Arpita Biswas
Assistant Professor, Department of Computer Science, Rutgers School of Arts and Sciences
Researchers examined five years of hourly electricity generation, demand and emissions data from the Energy Information Administration starting July 1, 2018. They focused on the 13 geographic regions in the United States.
With this
dataset
, the researchers constructed a statistical model to explore how increases in hourly solar energy generation would affect CO2 emissions within a given region and in its neighboring regions.
The study quantified both immediate and delayed emissions reductions resulting from added solar generation. For example, the researchers found that in California, a 15% increase in solar power at noon was associated with a reduction of 147.18 metric tons of CO2 in the region in the first hour and 16.08 metric tons eight hours later.
“It was rewarding to see how advanced computational modeling can uncover not just the immediate, but also the delayed and far-reaching spillover effects of solar energy adoption,” said the lead author
Arpita Biswas
, an assistant professor with the Department of Computer Science at the Rutgers School of Arts and Sciences. “From a computer science perspective, this study demonstrates the power of harnessing large-scale, high-resolution energy data to generate actionable insights. For policymakers and investors, it offers a roadmap for targeting solar investments where emissions reductions are most impactful and where solar energy infrastructure can yield the highest returns.”
The researchers said their methods provide a more nuanced understanding of system-level impacts from solar expansion than previous studies, pinpointing where the benefits of increased solar energy adoption could best be realized. In some areas, such as California, Florida, the mid-Atlantic, the Midwest, Texas and the Southwest, small increases in solar were estimated to deliver large CO2 reductions, while in others, such as New England, the central U.S., and Tennessee, impacts were found to be minimal – even at much larger increases in solar generation.
In addition, the researchers said their study demonstrates the significant spillover effects solar adoption has on neighboring regions, highlighting the value of coordinated clean energy efforts. For example, a 15% increase in solar capacity in California was associated with a reduction of 913 and 1,942 metric tons of CO2 emissions per day in the northwest and southwest regions, respectively.
“
I am very excited about this study because it harnesses the power of data science to offer insights for policymakers and stakeholders in achieving CO2 reduction targets through increased solar generation,” said Francesca Dominici, director of the Harvard Data Science Initiative and Clarence James Gamble Professor of Biostatistics, Population and Data Science and a corresponding author of the study.

• [技术贡献] **rdtsc** 提供了与绿色能源优化相关的GitHub项目链接，为有兴趣进一步研究或处理数据的人提供了技术支持。

• [批评与质疑] **m0llusk** 通过提及德国露台太阳能的普及，暗示这种基于数据的预测可能无法完全捕捉技术和社会趋势，质疑研究预测的全面性。

• [全面批评] **m101** 对研究的整体思路提出批评，认为仅仅关注二氧化碳排放和太阳能是不够全面的，主张要从更广泛的角度看待所有发电技术，并认为太阳能并非解决气候变化的核心方案，甚至可能是一种“干扰”。

补充讨论：
• [对研究内容的期望] **sophia01** 和 **metonymy** 对文章中提到的“地图”感到困惑或失望，因为他们期待看到实际的地图展示，但文章似乎没有提供。

• [无关评论] **lorenzohess** 提到了一个与讨论主题无关的内容（"On Mercury"），并未对研究或观点做出实际贡献。

• [研究资助背景] **searine** 指出了研究的资助来源，强调该研究得到了美国纳税人资助的多个拨款以及哈佛大学的机构支持，可能意在强调研究的权威性或透明度。

争议焦点：
• 研究是否全面：部分评论（如 **m0llusk** 和 **m101**）质疑研究的预测能力及其对整体环境问题的适用性，认为太阳能只是其中一个方面，而非唯一解决方案。
• 地区差异：不同地区太阳能发电的效果差异显著，这一发现引发了对政策制定和能源规划的进一步思考（**pards** 的评论）。

data.title: Ergonomic keyboarding with the Svalboard: a half-year retrospective
data.author: Twey
data.article_summary: 本文作者讲述了自己作为计算机重度使用者，从18岁开始出现重复性劳损（RSI）症状，并通过切换到Dvorak键盘布局缓解了问题。此后17年一直使用Dvorak布局。作者对人机交互特别感兴趣，尝试了多种键盘，包括微软人体工学键盘和Kinesis Advantage，最终选择了Ergodox EZ键盘。该键盘具备分离式设计、帐篷状结构和拇指簇键等特点，有效缓解了作者的腕部和肘部疼痛。作者还强调了键盘可编程性的重要性，特别是为了适应个人习惯和速记（stenography）需求。此外，作者提到对CharaChorder这种通过减少手指移动和弦式输入来提高打字速度的设备感兴趣，但因其操作系统封闭、配置限制而未能深入开发新的速记理论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： ergonomic键盘设计及其使用体验

不同观点：
• **关于手指运动的 ergonomic 效果**：
  - [ssfrr] 质疑最小化手指运动是否真的符合 ergonomic 原则，认为重复性（repetitive）是RSI（重复性劳损）的关键，而非仅仅运动幅度。他以钢琴演奏者为例，指出大幅度的手部运动虽然消耗更多能量，但并不一定导致更多伤害。
  
• **协作中的使用不便**：
  - [j1elo] 提出当其他人需要临时使用电脑时，专用 ergonomic 设备（如特殊轨迹球或键盘）可能造成不便，因为其他人不熟悉这些设备的操作方式，可能影响协作效率。

• **市场与价格问题**：
  - [eviks] 提到从普通的非 ergonomic 键盘到 split 键盘的过渡是合理的，但健康问题导致的市场需求过于小众且昂贵。他质疑为何没有便宜的橡胶圆顶 split 键盘，认为这样的产品可以提供一定的健康优势而不必付出高昂的机械成本。
  - [burnt-resistor] 提到90年代的DataHand Pro II因价格过高而未能普及，认为如果价格在150-250美元之间可能会更成功。

• **个人长期使用体验**：
  - [donio] 作为使用了DataHand超过25年的用户，分享了自己对设备的长期使用和维护经验，并对新型设备（Svalboard）表示兴趣，特别是对硬件和手感的评价。
  - [RDaneel0livaw] 表示自己从小喜欢 split ergonomic 键盘，尤其钟爱带有南向数字键盘的设计，并将其用于游戏。

• **健康问题与解决方案**：
  - [aorth] 描述了自己因打字导致的指尖疼痛问题，寻求实际的解决方案，如拉伸、加强锻炼或改变饮食，以期长期保持手部健康。

• **个人键盘体验与选择**：
  - [floren] 分享了自己从 split ortholinear 键盘（ergodox）转回传统设计键盘后，手部疼痛问题得到缓解的经历，暗示找到适合自己的键盘设计可能比单纯追求 ergonomic 设计更重要。
  - [jiehong] 也分享了自己从 ergodox 转向 Kinesis Advantage 360 的体验，并提到使用语音输入作为辅助。

补充讨论：
• **对专用设备的依赖性顾虑**：
  - [Fraterkes] 担心过于习惯特定 ergonomic 设备（如Svalboard）后，在使用普通笔记本电脑时会感到不便和困扰。
  
• **技术类比**：
  - [Already__Taken] 提到键盘触发机制与高端漆弹枪的调节机制类似，提供了一种技术上的类比视角。

争议焦点：
• **最小化手指运动的 ergonomic 效果**：不同用户对是否应最小化手指运动存在不同看法，有人认为重复性运动是导致RSI的主因，而非运动幅度本身。

44759171.article_content:
My background
Â§
E
ven before I started pressing buttons for a living I was always a
pretty heavy computer user.  When I was about 18 I started
experiencing symptoms of RSI.  At around the same time I learnt of the
Dvorak keyboard layout, and so I switched, hoping it would solve my
problems.  It did, at least at the time, and so for the last 17 years
Iâve been a Dvorak user.
A
t the same time Iâm really interested in human/machine interaction
and ways to get the contents of the human brain into a machine as
fluently as possible.  As a combined result of these two factors, I
worked my way through a few different physical keyboards, including
the Microsoft Ergonomic series (which I struggled to make Windows 2000
recognize â go figure) and a Kinesis Advantage, but my keyboard of
choice for many years now has been the
Ergodox EZ
.  The Ergodox (and its ZSA
comrade the Moonlander) is a solid keyboard, with a few features that
Iâve come to realize are very important:
Split halves
. Any keyboard with the halves joined together (that is
narrower than shoulder-width, as is the case with every joined
keyboard Iâve seen so far) causes the elbows to bend in and the wrists
to bend out, which seems to be the primary trigger of wrist pain
for me.
Tenting
. Ditto for the elbows: last year I found myself struggling
with pain and numbness in my arm that, on investigation, matched
symptoms of early cubital tunnel syndrome.  Tenting, rotating the
halves of the keyboard so that the wrists sit in a slight angle,
allows the elbows to rest in a more natural slightly-bent position,
and since adopting it I havenât had any further problems with my elbow.
Figure 1. The Microsoft Ergonomic Keyboard.
Thumb clusters
. The first symptom I got was whatâs affectionately
known as âemacs pinkyâ.
In fact, on most keyboards (though sadly no longer on ThinkPads) the control key, positioned in the bottom-right corner, can and should be held with the palm â this makes some combinations more awkward, though no more awkward than with the little finger, and saves the weakest digit.  In fact, I think it would be better named for vi â the escape key is perhaps the least ergonomic key on a standard keyboard.  Some people like to put it in the place of caps-lock, which is of course entirely missing the point.
The
reason I picked up the Kinesis Advantage is that on these keyboards
the thumb, which is highly underutilized in standard layouts, gets a
dedicated cluster of keys, perfect for things like modifiers, since
the opposable thumbs donât limit the motion of the rest of the hand at
all, no matter how itâs engaged.
Figure 2. The Kinesis Advantage.  This one is wireless, while mine, the original model, was connected by PS/2 cable.  But the layout hasnât changed.
Programmability
. My customization is light compared to some
peopleâs, but my keyboard usage is pretty idiosyncratic, so itâs
important to me to be able to customize my keyboard when I need to.
Particularly for keyboards with fewer keys that need heavier layer
usage, I want to be able to set up the layers as I want.  My most
elaborate customization is that I am (from time to time) a hobbyist
stenographer
, and rather
than having a separate device I find it convenient to be able to
configure my keyboard to speak one of the steno protocols understood
by
Plover
such as TX
Bolt or GeminiPR.
Finger-oriented keyboarding
Â§
W
ith this in mind, I was pretty excited when I stumbled across the
CharaChorder
.  The promise is
simple: increase typing speed through a combination of minimizing
finger movement and stenography-style chording (albeit with a theory
designed to have a shallower learning curve, basically just mashing
all the letters of the word at once).  I signed up to the
pre-order, and when I got it I immediately started playing around,
practising a few hours per day on the (very good!) training software.
Figure 3. The CharaChorder One.
I
f youâve ever done typing training, youâll know that most of the
point of the drills and forms that they teach you is to keep your
fingers on the home row so that you can reach all the letters with a
minimum of movement.  The CharaChorder turns this on its head: on the
CharaChorder there is
only
the home row.  Where you would stretch up
or down or sideways to reach a key on a traditional keyboard, on the
CharaChorder you simply wiggle a joystick in that direction, never
taking your finger off the key.
There is in fact a second row of joysticks used for arrow keys or mouse emulation, but weâll ignore them for the purposes of this since they donât impact most of the typing experience.
I
loved the compact form factor combined with the power of chording,
and I was excited to develop a new steno theory based on the
CharaChorderâs unique structure.  Unfortunately, I was thwarted: the
CC1 runs the CharaChorder OS, a closed-source project with only a
restricted set of chording configurations, and the fact that it must
take place

data.title: Coffeematic PC – A coffee maker computer that pumps hot coffee to the CPU
data.author: dougdude3339
data.article_summary: 《COFFEEMATIC PC》是由艺术家Doug MacDowell创作的一台结合了咖啡机与电脑功能的独特设备。该设备使用了一台1980年代的通用电气（GE）滴漏式咖啡机作为机箱，内部安装了由回收零件和新增硬件组成的电脑系统，包括ASUS主板、AMD处理器、DDR2内存、固态硬盘和Radeon显卡，运行Linux Mint操作系统。咖啡机部分仍能正常煮咖啡，而电脑部分则通过一个泵将热咖啡循环，以帮助冷却CPU。虽然使用热咖啡进行冷却听起来具有破坏性，但系统能够达到平衡，且不会崩溃。这个项目是咖啡机电脑改造系列中的一部分，最早的类似项目出现在2002年。Coffeematic PC的最大创新在于利用咖啡循环实现电脑冷却，体现了技术与日常物品的创意结合。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕将咖啡机与PC结合的创意项目的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• jfengel：建议将水泵入CPU降温后再通过咖啡粉，但指出咖啡的理想冲泡温度高于CPU安全温度，建议二次加热。
• Groxx：赞赏项目的创意和实用性。
• yupyupyups：幽默地提到运行Electron应用会导致咖啡变冷，暗示Electron应用的资源消耗问题。
• Lio：建议通过AI扩展项目，让系统推测用户想要的饮品，并带有幽默的《银河系漫游指南》风格。
• bitcrshr：提到HTTP 418状态码（愚人节玩笑），暗示项目本身的趣味性。
• zeta0134：认为这是一个有趣的 silly 项目，并指出咖啡不仅作为机箱的一部分，还能充当有效的散热器。
• nanomonkey：分享了自己在管理GPU集群时想利用废热进行酒精蒸馏的经历，认为GPU和酒精蒸馏很匹配。
• bluelightning2k：调侃项目与Java的兼容性。
• TZubiri：以幽默的方式讨论了GE Coffeemattic PC与GNU系统的关系，指出该项目实际上是GNU系统的一部分。
• 9front：建议使用"Coffee Linux"作为操作系统，而不是"Linux Mint"，继续项目的幽默基调。
• ghm2180：提出一个带有触觉反馈的按键设计，按下时运行CPU/GPU，并根据水温提供反馈，以提示水何时加热完成。
• iammrpayments：担心管道材质在加热水后是否适合饮用。
• reboot81：表示自己正在忙于修复一辆鱼缸自行车，但有意制作类似的项目。
• dabumere：简单表达了项目带来的愉快感受。
• bawana：质疑设计的合理性，指出咖啡渣可能堵塞散热器和冷却块，并提出使用RO水和去除散热器的替代方案。

补充讨论：
• 项目创意的趣味性和实用性是讨论的核心，不少人对项目的创意表示赞赏。
• 关于设计合理性的争议，主要集中在咖啡渣可能导致的堵塞和腐蚀问题，以及水管材料是否适合饮用。
• 不同用户对项目的扩展建议（如AI、触觉反馈、操作系统命名）增加了讨论的趣味性和多样性。
• 部分评论通过幽默和引用（如HTTP 418和GNU/Linux）增添了对话的轻松氛围。

44762880.article_content:
COFFEEMATIC PC
A coffee maker computer by Doug MacDowell artist
Sometime during winter 2024, I found myself at a thrift store. I was
staring at rows of appliances, wrapped in plastic and clinging to
life, trying to answer one question: which of these is the right
chassis for a retro gaming computer?
Driving home, I took corners carefully, checking that the General
Electric (GE) drip coffee maker I’d chosen was safe in the backseat.
The coffee maker's given name was Coffeematic. Circa 1980, it is boxy
yet athletic – unfazed by any considerations of future internet
connectivity. Best, it is perfect for being hacked.
Coffeematic is now Coffeematic PC – part gaming computer, part coffee
maker. A newly synthesized machine percolating processes well beyond
its original configuration.
Coffeematic PC is part of a lineage of coffee maker computers made
since 2002
. I'll describe that fascinating lineage here, and how it inspired an
art exhibition called
Sparklines
where hand-drafted data visualizations accompany Coffeematic PC.
Profound and poetically articulated. Elegant and assertive. Highly
scaleable with dynamic acceleration. No. These do not describe
Coffeematic PC or its peers (one of those phrases describes a bottle
of wine.) A custom built computer can be basic and functional, or an
elaborate, absurd, spinning piece of art.
Coffeematic PC falls somewhere in that spectrum while also being
nearly self-destructive.
This is how Coffeematic PC works.
The computer is fully functional. The coffee maker is too
, it percolates Java like a regular coffee maker. Very hot Java.
Computers usually use fans or liquid cooling systems to reduce heat.
Coffeematic PC uses the hot Java it brews to heat? cool? caffeinate?
the computer. A pump takes the hot, caffenated slurry (~90C/194F) and
circulates it thru two radiators sitting on top of Coffeematic PC's
crown -> down to a central processing unit (CPU) tucked within an ASUS
M2NPV-VM motherboard snugly strapped to Coffeematic PC's back. Java
continues through an artery returning to Coffeematic PC's caraffe. The
process repeats until Java is integrated with the user or the machine
is powered off.
↑ Coffeematic PC has a dedicated pump to aggressively dispense Java
for user.
CPU's are meant to be cool and Java hot.
Despite circulating hot Java, Coffeematic PC does not crash.
To understand more, I wrote command line code to gather data on
Coffeematic PC every 5 seconds, and monitored Coffeematic PC for 75
minutes. The graph below shows the results. The machine is just barely
non-destructive.
Coffeematic PC's CPU, body, and circulatory system eventually find
equilibrium. A warm 33C/91F - amazingly close to the temperature of
the slurry that flows through you and me.
An important part of this project is the lineage of coffee maker
computers. Before discussing that,
this is how Coffeematic PC was made.
The build is a mix of discarded electronics and newly purchased
hardware, pumps, and radiators. The motherboard, CPU, RAM, and
graphics card are from the mid 2000's and were sourced from a
recycling center. This is a parts list for Coffeematic PC.
GE Coffeematic Coffee Maker 10 Cup
ASUS M2NPV-VM AM2 Motherboard
AMD Athlon II X4 640 3 GHz Quad-Core OEM/Tray Processor
Hynix 1GB 2Rx8 PC2-5300U-555-12 PC2-DDR2 RAM
Acer SA100 240 GB 2.5" Solid State Drive
HIS H467QR1GH Radeon HD 4670 1 GB Video Card
Antec Earthwatts Green 430 W 80+ Bronze Certified ATX Power
Supply
Linux Mint Operating System
CPU Water Cooling Block for Intel
Water Cooling Computer Radiator

44762880.article_summary: 《COFFEEMATIC PC》是由艺术家Doug MacDowell创作的一台结合了咖啡机与电脑功能的独特设备。该设备使用了一台1980年代的通用电气（GE）滴漏式咖啡机作为机箱，内部安装了由回收零件和新增硬件组成的电脑系统，包括ASUS主板、AMD处理器、DDR2内存、固态硬盘和Radeon显卡，运行Linux Mint操作系统。咖啡机部分仍能正常煮咖啡，而电脑部分则通过一个泵将热咖啡循环，以帮助冷却CPU。虽然使用热咖啡进行冷却听起来具有破坏性，但系统能够达到平衡，且不会崩溃。这个项目是咖啡机电脑改造系列中的一部分，最早的类似项目出现在2002年。Coffeematic PC的最大创新在于利用咖啡循环实现电脑冷却，体现了技术与日常物品的创意结合。
44762880.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕将咖啡机与PC结合的创意项目的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• jfengel：建议将水泵入CPU降温后再通过咖啡粉，但指出咖啡的理想冲泡温度高于CPU安全温度，建议二次加热。
• Groxx：赞赏项目的创意和实用性。
• yupyupyups：幽默地提到运行Electron应用会导致咖啡变冷，暗示Electron应用的资源消耗问题。
• Lio：建议通过AI扩展项目，让系统推测用户想要的饮品，并带有幽默的《银河系漫游指南》风格。
• bitcrshr：提到HTTP 418状态码（愚人节玩笑），暗示项目本身的趣味性。
• zeta0134：认为这是一个有趣的 silly 项目，并指出咖啡不仅作为机箱的一部分，还能充当有效的散热器。
• nanomonkey：分享了自己在管理GPU集群时想利用废热进行酒精蒸馏的经历，认为GPU和酒精蒸馏很匹配。
• bluelightning2k：调侃项目与Java的兼容性。
• TZubiri：以幽默的方式讨论了GE Coffeemattic PC与GNU系统的关系，指出该项目实际上是GNU系统的一部分。
• 9front：建议使用"Coffee Linux"作为操作系统，而不是"Linux Mint"，继续项目的幽默基调。
• ghm2180：提出一个带有触觉反馈的按键设计，按下时运行CPU/GPU，并根据水温提供反馈，以提示水何时加热完成。
• iammrpayments：担心管道材质在加热水后是否适合饮用。
• reboot81：表示自己正在忙于修复一辆鱼缸自行车，但有意制作类似的项目。
• dabumere：简单表达了项目带来的愉快感受。
• bawana：质疑设计的合理性，指出咖啡渣可能堵塞散热器和冷却块，并提出使用RO水和去除散热器的替代方案。

补充讨论：
• 项目创意的趣味性和实用性是讨论的核心，不少人对项目的创意表示赞赏。
• 关于设计合理性的争议，主要集中在咖啡渣可能导致的堵塞和腐蚀问题，以及水管材料是否适合饮用。
• 不同用户对项目的扩展建议（如AI、触觉反馈、操作系统命名）增加了讨论的趣味性和多样性。
• 部分评论通过幽默和引用（如HTTP 418和GNU/Linux）增添了对话的轻松氛围。

data.title: Slow
data.author: calvinfo
data.article_summary: 这篇文章列举了人类需要极长时间才能完成的一些杰出项目，重点关注有明确目标的计划，如科学实验和建筑，而非去中心化或非计划性的变化。这些长期项目包括费马大定理的证明、建造超过百年的教堂如巴黎圣母院和圣家堂、自1978年开始的 Cape Grim 空气档案、1948年启动的弗雷明翰心脏研究、自1659年至今的中英格兰温度记录、1967年开始设计并在2016年首次观测到引力波的LIGO探测器、1988年启动的E. coli长期进化实验、1927年开始的沥青滴漏实验、旨在持续一万年的万年钟，以及纽约第二大道地铁项目，其准备工作始于1942年，首阶段于2017年开通。文章还提及了世界上最古老的公司和一些其他长期研究项目，并提出一个问题：哪些项目确实需要长时间，哪些可以加速完成？
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多代项目与长期实验的性质，以及项目拖延的原因和合理性。

不同观点：
• **长期规划与多代项目的价值**：[lubujackson]通过牛津大学主梁更换的故事展示了前人为后代着想的长远规划。[tombert]提到了试图证明Collatz猜想的个人努力，认为即使失败也是有价值的，因为数学是代代相传的积累。[aaronbrethorst]则批评了曼哈顿第二大道地铁项目的拖延，指出其成本高昂且不必要。

• **项目拖延的原因**：[aaronbrethorst]和[rangestransform]指出，第二大道地铁项目的拖延主要是由于政治因素和管理不善，而非技术问题。[rangestransform]特别强调了政治斗争和管理低效是导致项目拖延和成本增加的主要原因。[bee_rider]则区分了本质上需要长时间的项目（如沥青滴漏实验）和因为缺乏资源而拖延的项目（如 Notre Dame 教堂的建造）。

• **科学与研究的长期性**：[dfabulich]通过宇宙距离阶梯的例子展示了科学研究中需要长时间积累和精确测量的过程。[Bukhmanizer]用一个讽刺的漫画指出了人们对高质量科学研究的急功近利心态。[brudgers]和[m463]提到《计算机程序设计艺术》这本自1962年以来一直在编写中的书，强调了有些项目需要长时间的打磨。

• **政治体制对长期项目的影响**：[hermitcrab]讨论了民主制度和集权制度在长期项目规划上的优缺点，指出民主制度下政治家更关注短期选举周期，而集权制度则可能进行更长远的规划但缺乏领导层的和平更替机制。

补充讨论：
• **项目的加速可能性**：[MontyCarloHall]认为大多数研究项目由于其本质无法加速，但指出第二大道地铁和圣家堂这类项目本可以加速，却被拖延了多年。

• **对“快速”项目的批评**：[rglover]提到对快速项目的批评，认为有些团队和项目故意放慢速度是有其合理性的，不应被贬低。

• **历史与现代项目的对比**：评论中多次提到历史上的科学实验和建筑项目，与现代项目进行对比，突出了现代项目中由于政治和管理问题导致的拖延。

争议焦点：
• 第二大道地铁项目的拖延原因及责任归属。
• 项目加速的可行性与合理性。
• 不同政治体制对长期项目的影响优劣。

通过这些观点，评论展示了长期项目在不同领域和背景下的复杂性，以及影响其成功的多种因素。

44748934.article_content:
misc
sb
What problems can human beings
only
solve over a very long period of time? And how can we build institutions that solve those problems?
Below is a list of marvellous projects which human beings have undertaken over an exceptionally long time. Many examples contributed by people on
Twitter
.
The focus is on goal-directed projects (e.g., a scientific experiment or a building), less on more decentralized or unplanned changes (e.g., languages, domestication of livestock, cities, religions). Of course, those are also fascinating, but they have less of a sense of a long-term goal. Jericho is incredible, but the founders probably weren't thinking "I hope this is still here in 9,000 years".
This page is a
riff on Patrick Collison's list of /fast projects
. There are surprisingly many commonalities with those projects.
The proof of Fermat's Last Theorem involved an incredible amount of mathematics developed over decades and centuries:
wikipedia
.
Many Cathedrals were built over more than a century. An example is
Notre Dame
, over 1163-1345. There are many more.
An ongoing example is the
Sagrada Familia
, begun in 1882, and continuing today.
The
Cape Grim Air Archive
, which has been archiving air since 1978, so later researchers can conduct longitudinal studies.
The
Framingham Heart Study
, a longitudinal study of the heart which began in 1948.
The
Central England Temperature series
, from 1659 to the present.
The early designs for the
LIGO gravitational wave detector
were developed in 1967; the instrument itself was developed over many decades, and first saw gravitational waves in 2016
1
.
The
E. coli long-term evolution experiment
, from 1988 to the present.
The
pitch drop experiment
from 1927 to the present
2
.
The
Clock of the Long Now
, which aspires to last 10,000 years.
I suspect many key open source systems (Linux, Wikipedia) will still be around in 100 years. I won't be surprised if certain standards still show up in a thousand years, perhaps in a modified form. ASCII gives rise to Unicode gives rise to [???] Will Unix Time or TCP/IP ever be replaced? Modified: sure. But there's at least some chance they'll be with us for millenia.
The
2nd Ave Subway in Manhattan
, with preparatory construction beginning in 1942. First phase opened in 2017.
The
list of oldest companies in the world
is food for thought. Sad to report the 2006 demise of
Kongo Gumi
, which began in 578. It was in the construction business, originally of Shinto Shrines (I believe). Such Shrines undergo a continuous process of renewal; an example is the
Izumo-taisha
, which may date to BCE.
The
Study of Mathematically Precocious Youth
, begun in 1971, and continuing as of 2025 (contributed by Tom McCarthy)
Wikipedia lists
many other long-term exeriments
.
A fun question: of these projects, which
required
a long time, and which could have been greatly accelerated?
Footnotes
In 1998 I went to a talk by Kip Thorne where he said LIGO would likely need a strain sensitivity of "1 part in 10 to the 21" to see anything. That's an accuracy comparable to measuring the distance to the Sun to an accuracy of one atom. I laughed, and thought it would take centuries, at least. In the second sentence of the abstract of the 2016 paper they report a strain sensitivity of
1.0 \times
10^{-21}
.
↩︎
My office was for many years in the same building as the pitch drop experiment, and I would often walk past it multiple times a day. It has a slow but steady psychological impact in how you think about the space of projects open to you. This is fitting.
↩︎

data.title: How to make almost anything (2019)
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: D. Sculley，谷歌剑桥机器学习团队负责人，参与一个涉及机器学习在设计和制造领域应用的课程。他对跨领域机会特别感兴趣，包括生物学和化学空间。Sculley自2003年开始从事机器学习，之前有教育和艺术背景。课程为期14周，每周聚焦不同主题，从CAD和草图设计到嵌入式编程、网络、机械加工等，最终完成一个项目。Sculley计划每周参与项目，乐于讨论机器学习相关问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕MIT的"How to Make Almost Anything"课程及其相关内容的讨论，涉及课程内容、个人制造能力、技能广度与深度等。

不同观点：
• [支持与赞赏课程]
  ◦ [criddell] 认为这是个人制造的黄金时代，高品质的个人制造能力已经实现，Neil Gershenfeld的预言正在成真。
  ◦ [zakqwy] 以亲身经历表示该课程非常有趣，涵盖了数字制造和微控制器等内容。
  ◦ [jeffreyw128] 表示这是他大学期间最喜欢的课程。
  ◦ [low_tech_punk] 和 [sgnelson] 提供了课程的链接和进一步资源，强调学生文档和项目是课程亮点。

• [对课程内容的批评与扩展建议]
  ◦ [moron4hire] 批评课程缺乏基础技能如木工、金属加工、管道、混凝土等，认为课程视野狭窄，并指出科技行业过度贬低年长者的技能和经验。
  ◦ [probably_wrong] 认为课程遗漏了缝纫等技能，建议将课程名称改为"How to make some things (most of which require a computer)"。

• [个人经验与反思]
  ◦ [dhosek] 后悔在本科期间没有选修某些实践类课程，如自制工具课程。
  ◦ [Animats] 回忆TechShop的时代，认为课程像是快速浏览多个技能，但要精通某项技能需要更多时间。

• [其他相关课程推荐]
  ◦ [car] 推荐MIT的合成生物学课程"How to Grow (Almost) Anything"，并分享了课程链接。

补充讨论：
• [LarsDu88] 提到PCB设计和从中国定制PCB价格波动的问题，认为美国初创公司有机会填补这一市场空缺。
• [westurner] 指出课程"Week 8: Molding and Casting"的链接404错误，并建议新的材料和科技主题如可编程物质、纳米自组装、AI材料设计等。

争议焦点：
• 课程内容的广度与深度：[moron4hire] 和 [probably_wrong] 认为课程缺乏基础技能和手工技能，而其他人如 [criddell] 和 [zakqwy] 则赞赏课程的创新性和实用性。

My name is D. Sculley.  I lead several teams at Google in
Cambridge doing research in various aspects of machine learning.
I'm involved in this course because many of our current projects involve
the use of machine learning for design or fabrication problems of
one form or another, including in the biology space and the chemistry
space.  I'm interested in learning more about other forms of fabrication
and seeing if there are interesting cross-domain opportunities to
think about.
Here is my
Google Scholar page
, if you're interested in ML papers.
As background, I started working in ML in about 2003.  Before that,
I spent several years in education working as a teacher, and before that
I was a V.E.S. ("art") major in undergrad.
I'll be working on class projects each week, and am planning on making
plenty of mistakes. Always happy to talk about machine learning if that's of interest.

44776434.article_content:
The Fulbright Program: Chock Full of Bright Ideas
Tags:
academia
,
research
,
musings
Published on
Friday, August 1, 2025
« Previous post:
There is Fun in the Fundamentals
One of the most memorable events in my career so far was being selected
as a host for the
Fulbright Program
.
When
Emily (Simons)
approached me with her idea
of applying for this type of scholarship, I was already blown away by
her enthusiasm—but little did I imagine how immensely enriching her
visit to
the lab
would turn out to be!
We initially discussed a project aligned with our shared interest in
healthcare topics; specifically, I proposed making Emily part of
a planned project with cardiologists, the aim being to study circulatory failure
via certain machine learning methods. The project fell through,
however, since our collaborators were unable to provide data due to
privacy concerns.
1
Hence, we pivoted, and I suggested a couple of
other projects that Emily might be interested in.
Having developed a taste for all things graphs and networks, it was only
a matter of time before Emily started contributing to our work on
physician–patient referral networks
,
showing her skills in data science and visualization. Working together
with
Jeremy (Wayland)
, Emily quickly also got
enthralled by our efforts to better understand
datasets in graph learning. She and Jeremy thus joined a project that
Corinna (Coupette)
and I had been dreaming of
for some time. As an intrepid fellowship, we finally brought it to
fruition as our joint ICML 2025 paper
No Metric to Rule Them All: Toward Principled Evaluations of Graph-Learning Datasets
.
2
This was already outstanding, but Emily did not stop there! Like a
breath of fresh air, she also started working on dissemination strategies for
our projects, improved our repositories, and helped revamp our website.
Watching her grow as a researcher, writer, and software
developer was truly awe-inspiring. And, from what I can
tell, the research stay was rewarding for her as well. New friends, new
colleagues, new experiences—these are things that cannot (and
should not) be easily quantified.
So
why
am I writing all of this? There are two reasons: First, Emily is
on the job market and I cannot sing her praises highly enough. Second,
this is a time of uncertainty; a time in which funding is cut, in
particular for programs that may not yield direct results. Are the
United States richer or better off because of our joint research projects? Probably not—or maybe not
yet
. Like any type of fundamental
research, our projects are but a small part of the grand and eternal
conversation that is science.
It is precisely for this reason that we must resist the urge to see
everything as a
commodity
or as a
fungible good
. The true value of
the Fulbright Program lies in connecting bright minds with others and
giving them new opportunities.
This brings about changes whose
beneficial consequences we cannot possibly fathom in the moment.
To misquote
Boethius
:
And it is because you don’t know the end and purpose of things that
you think these programs have no worth.
Through the Fulbright Program, we all got to meet someone we would not
have met otherwise. Through the Fulbright Program, we created
connections that would not have happened otherwise. Through the
Fulbright Program, we have all been intellectually enriched. I hope
that the politicians responsible for these programs see them for what they
are, i.e., a
unique
opportunity to foster change, innovation, and
mutual understanding across cultural barriers. I, for one, would love to
support such a program.
Let us not sell
tomorrow
in a feeble attempt
to save money
today
.
In my experience, this is the number one reason why research projects fail in Germany; maybe this will be the subject of a subsequent post.
↩︎
For more Tolkien references concerning this work, please read
Emily’s highly engaging blog post
.
↩︎

data.title: The Ski Rental Problem
data.author: skywalqer
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了滑雪租赁问题，这是一个经典的在线算法问题。问题场景是：你去滑雪，但不确定会滑多少天，租滑雪设备每天1单位货币，而购买则需B单位货币。目标是决定是否以及何时购买滑雪设备。

**离线最优算法**：如果提前知道滑雪天数k，当k ≥ B时应购买，k < B时应租。总费用为min{k, B}。

**简单在线算法**：不知道k时，可以先租，直到租金达到B时购买。这种方法的最坏情况成本是两倍于离线最优算法，即竞争比为2。

**随机化算法**：文章进一步探讨了一种随机化算法，通过选择适当的概率分布P(x)，使得期望竞争比接近于$\frac{e}{e-1}$。核心思想是找到一种概率分布，使得期望成本与最优成本的比值（竞争比）不随k变化，从而优化算法性能。经过推导，得出P(x)应为指数分布，满足$\int_0^\infty P(x)dx = 1$。

最终，随机化算法能提供更好的平均性能，适合多次决策场景。

Ski Rental Problem
The ski rental problem is a classic example problem in online algorithms. It feels like a small but interesting problem that can be explained relatively easily while some clever tricks can be applied to it.
In this article, I took
these lecture notes
by Debmalya Panigrahi and Hangjie Ji and tried to rewrite them in a way that is easier to understand (at least for me).
Formulation
You are going skiing in the mountains but you are unsure about the weather reports and don't know how many days you will want to ski (and it can be any number of days).
Renting skis costs $1$ unit of currency while buying them costs $B$ units of currency.
The question is whether you should buy skis and on which day.
Optimal offline algorithm
Assuming you wound know the number $k$ of days you will want to ski in advance, an optimal algorithm can be derived.
If $k \geq B$, you should buy the skis and if $k < B$, you should only rent them.
So you will pay $\min\{k, B\}$.
We will need this later, so let's call it $\text{opt}(k) = \min\{k, B\}$.
Simple online algorithm
But what about if you don't know $k$?
A simple algorithm is to buy the skis when you paid $B$ for renting them.
So, the cost is $$\text{alg}(k) = \begin{cases}k & \text{if }k\leq B\\ B+B & \text{if }k>B\end{cases}.$$
We will study the competitive ratio $\rho$ defined as the worst-case ratio of a given online algorithm and the optimal offline algorithm.
$$
\rho_\text{simple} = \max_k \frac{\text{alg(k)}}{\text{opt}(k)} = \max_k \begin{Bmatrix}\frac{k}{k} & \text{if }k \leq B\\ \frac{B+B}{B} & \text{if }k > B\end{Bmatrix} = \max_k \begin{Bmatrix}1 & \text{if }k \leq B\\ 2 & \text{if }k > B\end{Bmatrix} = 2
$$
So, the simple online algorithm is at most two times worse than the offline "future knowing" algorithm.
The randomized algorithm
Let's try to find a better performing randomized algorithm. In fact, an algorithm with $\mathbb{E}[\rho]\approx\frac{e}{e-1}$ exists. This could be useful for example if we do many such decisions and want to do well on average.
In this algorithm, we will buy skis on the $(i+1)$-th day with probability $P_i$. These probabilities should satisfy $\sum_{i=0}^\infty P_i = 1$. We will also assume that the ski buying events are independent.
So when we buy the skis on day $i+1$, we pay $i+B$ if $i < k$ and $k$ if $i \geq k$, thus the expected cost is:
$$
\mathbb{E}\left[\text{alg}(k)\right] = k\sum_{i\geq k}P_i + \sum_{i<k}(i+B)P_i
$$
We will approximate this with a continuous probability distribution with probability density $P(x)$:
$$
\mathbb{E}\left[\text{alg}(k)\right] \approx k\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + \int_0^k (x+B)P(x)\mathrm{d}x
$$
Thus, we have switched from a discrete algorithm to a continuous one, so it will tell us the exact time when to buy instead of some day. With it we will approximate the discrete solution (which also exists but is more complicated to analyze).
Now, we would like to find the optimal probability distribution $P(x)$ such that the competitive ratio $\rho$ is the lowest. We will use an insight which we won't prove. The insight is that the optimal choice is such a distribution $P(x)$ that $\alpha = \frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\text{alg}(k)\right]}{\text{opt}(k)}$ does not depend on $k$. Thus, $\mathbb{E}\left[\rho\right] = \max_k\frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\text{alg}(k)\right]}{\text{opt}(k)} = \max_k\alpha = \alpha$.
So, we have
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\text{alg}(k)\right]}{\text{opt}(k)} &= \alpha \\
k\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + \int_0^k (x+B)P(x)\mathrm{d}x &= \alpha\min\{k, B\}
\end{aligned}
$$
And we have two cases,
I) When $k \geq B$
We differentiate both sides with respect to $k$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\global\def\der{\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}k}}
\global\def\Der#1{\frac{\mathrm{d}#1}{\mathrm{d}k}}
k\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + \int_0^k (x+B)P(x)\mathrm{d}x &= \alpha B \\
\der\left(k\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + \int_0^k (x+B)P(x)\mathrm{d}x\right) &= \Der{\alpha B} \\
\Der{k}\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + k\der\left(\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x\right) + \der\left(\int_0^k (x+B)P(x)\mathrm{d}x\right) &= 0 \\
\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x - kP(k) + (k+B)P(k) &= 0 \\
\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + BP(k) &= 0
\end{aligned}
$$
Because $P(x) \geq 0$, the integral is nonnegative. And because $B > 0$, the integral must be zero and $P(k) = 0$ in order to satisfy the equation.
II) When $k < B$
We proceed in a similar fashion:
$$
\begin{aligned}
k\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + \int_0^k (x+B)P(x)\mathrm{d}x &= \alpha k \\
\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + BP(k) &= \alpha
\end{aligned}
$$
However, now we take the derivative once more:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\der\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + \der BP(k) &= \Der{\alpha} \\
B\Der{P(k)} - P(k) &= 0
\end{aligned}
$$
This is a differential equation, which can be solved as $P(k) = Ae^\frac{k}{B}$, where $A$ is some constant.
We have the constraint that $\int_0^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x = 1$, so if we combine both cases, we get:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\in

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过系统思维或调整方式应对复杂性或变化

不同观点：
• Obscurity4340认为生活类似于一个应用程序，可以通过调整设置来逐渐改变状态。他使用滑块或步进器的比喻，强调了变化应该是渐进的，既能防止意外变化，又能在足够时间和力量下实现调制。

• amelius建议不要直接切换状态（即翻转开关），而是进行从0到1的平滑过渡，使人们更容易接受这种变化方式，强调渐进和软过渡的重要性。

• IAmGraydon分享了自己通过系统思维应对信息过载的经验。他认为通过理解系统的基本结构，可以将复杂的信息压缩成易于理解的模型，从而更轻松地处理复杂性。他推荐了《Thinking in Systems》这本书，以帮助其他人发展这种技能。

补充讨论：
• Obscurity4340和amelius的观点之间存在一定的联系，两者都强调了渐进变化的重要性，但amelius更具体地提出了软过渡的方式，以促进接受度。

• IAmGraydon的观点相对独立，强调了系统思维作为应对复杂性的工具，提供了一种宏观视角来理解和处理复杂系统。

• 争议的焦点可能在于如何最有效地处理复杂性和变化：是通过渐进的调整（如Obscurity4340和amelius所建议），还是通过系统思维的理解和建模（如IAmGraydon所分享）。

data.author: defo10
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了人工智能（A.I.）陪伴在应对孤独感方面的潜在价值。作者与同事发表了一篇论文，认为在某些情况下，A.I.可能比真人更能提供陪伴，尤其对孤独的人而言。然而，这一观点在学术界尤其是社会科学和人文领域引发了争议，许多人担心A.I.会取代真实的人际关系。尽管这些担忧合理，但作者认为对人工共情的全面否定可能反映了对孤独者需求的忽视。文章引用多项研究和书籍，强调了孤独对健康的严重影响，如增加心血管疾病和痴呆风险。随着老龄化问题加剧，孤独在老年人中尤为普遍。虽然富裕者可以支付陪伴费用，但对大多数人而言，真实的人类关注是稀缺的。因此，A.I.陪伴或可成为缓解孤独的一种可行方案。

不同观点：

• JKCalhoun认为，网络本身已经导致了某种程度的孤独感，网络浏览从来不是群体活动。
• disambiguation指出，目前对AI的相对好处和危害还没有明确的数据，AI的自主性和个人数据集中化可能导致滥用和剥削。
• Havoc认为，AI缺乏真实的情感和变化，无法作为真正的社交替代品。
• ants_everywhere认为，社交媒体已经展示了技术对社交行为的某些负面影响，AI可能会进一步加剧这些问题，如伪造人格和意见操纵。
• xlbuttplug2则持一种极端观点，认为对某些人来说，AI提供的满足感可能比现实生活中的社交更有吸引力。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到AI的“空洞性”和“自主性”问题，以及技术对人类社交行为的深层次影响。
• 有人担心AI会加剧孤独感，而不是缓解它，特别是通过虚假的社交互动和人格伪造。
• 对AI的潜在滥用和数据集中化问题也被提及，认为需要提前预见和规范潜在的危害。
• 有人提出，技术已经解决了无聊问题，但孤独感依然存在，且可能变得更加复杂。
