From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Theory on customer satisfaction
The
Kano model
is a theory for product development and
customer satisfaction
developed in the 1980s by
Noriaki Kano
. This model provides a framework for understanding how different features of a product or service impact customer satisfaction, allowing organizations to prioritize development efforts effectively. According to the Kano Model, customer preferences are classified into five distinct categories, each representing different levels of influence on satisfaction.
Categories
[
edit
]
These categories have been translated into English using various names (delighters/exciters, satisfiers, dissatisfiers, etc.), but all refer to the original articles written by Kano.
Must-be Quality
[
edit
]
These are the requirements that the customers expect and are taken for granted. When done well, customers are just neutral, but when done poorly, customers are very dissatisfied. Kano originally called these "Must-be’s" because they are the requirements that must be included and are the price of entry into a market.
Examples: In a car, a functioning brake is a must be quality. In a hotel, providing a clean room is a basic necessity. In a call center, greeting customers is a basic necessity.
One-dimensional Quality
[
edit
]
These attributes result in satisfaction when fulfilled and dissatisfaction when not fulfilled.  These are attributes that are spoken and the ones in which companies compete.  An example of this would be a milk package that is said to have ten percent more milk for the same price will result in customer satisfaction, but if it only contains six percent then the customer will feel misled and it will lead to dissatisfaction.
Examples: In a car, acceleration. Time taken to resolve a customer's issue in a call center. Waiting service at a hotel.
Attractive Quality
[
edit
]
These attributes provide satisfaction when achieved fully, but do not cause dissatisfaction when not fulfilled. These are attributes that are not normally expected, for example, a thermometer on a package of milk showing the temperature of the milk.  Since these types of attributes of quality unexpectedly delight customers, they are often unspoken.
Examples: In a car, advanced parking sensor and four wheel steering. In a callcenter, providing special offers and compensations to customers or the proactive escalation and instant resolution of their issue is an attractive feature. In a hotel, providing free food is an attractive feature.
Indifferent Quality
[
edit
]
These attributes refer to aspects that are neither good nor bad, and they do not result in customer satisfaction or customer dissatisfaction. For example, the thickness of the wax coating on a milk carton might be key to the design and manufacturing of the carton, but consumers are not even aware of the distinction. It is beneficial to identify these attributes in the product to suppress them and diminish production costs.
Examples: In a call center, highly polite speaking and very prompt responses might not be necessary to satisfy customers and might not be appreciated by them. The same applies to hotels.
Reverse Quality
[
edit
]
These attributes refer to a high degree of achievement resulting in dissatisfaction and to the fact that not all customers are alike.  For example, some customers prefer high-tech products, while others prefer the basic model of a product and will be dissatisfied if a product has too many extra features.
[
1
]
Examples: In a callcenter, using a lot of jargon, using excessive pleasantries, or using excessive scripts while talking to customers might be off-putting for them. In a hotel, producing elaborate photographs of the facilities that set high expectations which are then not satisfied upon visiting can dissatisfy the customers.

1. **基本质量（Must-be Quality）**：客户认为理所当然的要素，满足不会增加满意度，但不满足会导致强烈不满。例如，汽车的刹车功能。  
2. **一维质量（One-dimensional Quality）**：满足时增加满意度，不满足时导致不满。例如，汽车的加速性能。  
3. **魅力质量（Attractive Quality）**：满足时增加满意度，但不满足不会导致不满。例如，汽车的先进停车传感器。  
4. **无差异质量（Indifferent Quality）**：对客户满意度无影响。例如，牛奶盒蜡层的厚度。  
5. **反向质量（Reverse Quality）**：过度满足某些客户可能不喜欢的属性。例如，产品有过多额外功能。

客户期望会随时间变化，属性可能从魅力因素变为基本需求。

data.title: Caches: LRU vs. Random
data.author: gslin
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了缓存替换策略，比较了随机替换、LRU（最近最少使用）以及一种名为2-random的新策略。2-random策略是从两个随机选项中选择一个更近期使用的进行替换。结果显示，对于较小缓存，LRU表现略优于2-random；但对于较大缓存，2-random表现更好。与FIFO和纯随机策略相比，LRU和2-random都更优。文章还提到，由于LRU实现成本高，常使用伪LRU，并探讨了伪2-random和伪3-random的性能。总体而言，2-random在大缓存中表现出色，是LRU的有效替代方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：随机选择策略在缓存和负载均衡中的应用及其性能表现

不同观点：
• [bob1029] 认为使用两个随机选择（2-random）并仅在这些选择中使用LRU（最近最少使用）策略，可能比DIP（动态概率）策略更有效。他还将这种方法与进化算法中的锦标赛选择机制进行了类比，指出可以通过调整锦标赛大小来控制选择压力。此外，1v1的随机选择计算成本很低，不需要维护全局排序。

• [pvillano] 对使用随机性来延缓性能急剧下降（cliffs）的想法表示兴趣。他提到，当循环访问n+1个对象而缓存只能容纳n个对象时，LRU策略会导致每次查找都发生缓存缺失/驱逐，从而使缓存失效，性能急剧下降。而2-random策略可以将这种性能悬崖转化为缓坡，并带有一个长尾效应。他还推测，当人们试图通过循环访问n个项但额外数据超出寄存器容量时，可能会出现这种效应。

• [hinkley] 表示难以理解为何2-random在负载均衡中比leastconn（最少连接数）策略更有效。他认为在缓存中，随机策略优于其他启发式方法是可以理解的，但在负载均衡中的优势则不太直观。

补充讨论：
• 关于2-random策略在缓存和负载均衡中的不同表现存在争议，特别是在负载均衡中为何优于传统策略（如leastconn）的解释。
• 讨论中提到了随机选择策略在计算成本和性能优化上的潜在优势，尤其是在不需要全局排序的情况下。
• 对缓存性能悬崖的缓解以及随机策略带来的长尾效应进行了具体场景的假设和推测。

Once upon a time, my
computer architecture professor
mentioned that using a random eviction policy for caches really isn't so bad. That random eviction isn't bad can be surprising — if your cache fills up and you have to get rid of something, choosing the
least recently used (LRU)
is an obvious choice, since you're more likely to use something if you've used it recently. If you have a tight loop, LRU is going to be perfect as long as the loop fits in cache, but it's going to cause a miss every time if the loop doesn't fit. A random eviction policy degrades gracefully as the loop gets too big.
In practice, on real workloads, random tends to do worse than other algorithms. But what if we take two random choices (2-random) and just use LRU between those two choices?
Here are the relative miss rates we get for SPEC CPU
1
with a Sandy Bridge-like cache (
8-way associative
, 64k, 256k, and 2MB L1, L2, and L3 caches, respectively). These are ratios (algorithm miss rate : random miss rate); lower is better. Each cache uses the same policy at all levels of the cache.

L3 (2MB)
2-random

0.95
FIFO
0.96

Random and FIFO are both strictly worse than either LRU or 2-random. LRU and 2-random are pretty close, with LRU edging out 2-random for the smaller caches and 2-random edging out LRU for the larger caches.
To see if anything odd is going on in any individual benchmark, we can look at the raw results on each sub-benchmark. The L1, L2, and L3 miss rates are all plotted in the same column for each benchmark, below:
As we might expect, LRU does worse than 2-random when the miss rates are high, and better when the miss rates are low.
At this point, it's not clear if 2-random is beating LRU in L3 cache miss rates because it does better when the caches are large or because it does better because it's the third level in a hierarchical cache. Since a cache line that's being actively used in L1 or L2 isn't touched in L3, an eviction can happen from the L3 (which forces an eviction of both the L1 and L2) since, as far as the L3 is concerned, that line hasn't been used recently. This makes it less obvious that LRU is a good eviction policy for L3 cache.
To separate out the effects, let's look at the relative miss rates for a non-hierarchical (single level) vs. hierarchical caches at various sizes
2
. For the hierarchical cache, the L1 and L2 sizes are as above, 64k and 256k, and only the L3 cache size varies. Below, we've got the geometric means of the ratios
3
of how each policy does (over all SPEC sub-benchmarks, compared to random eviction). A possible downside to this metric is that if we have some very low miss rates, those could dominate the mean since small fluctuations will have a large effect on the ratio, but we can look the distribution of results to see if that's the case.
Sizes below 512k are missing for the hierarchical case because of the 256k L2 — we're using an inclusive L3 cache here, so it doesn't really make sense to have an L3 that's smaller than the L2. Sizes above 16M are omitted because cache miss rates converge when the cache gets too big, which is uninteresting.
Looking at the single cache case, it seems that LRU works a bit better than 2-random for smaller caches (lower miss ratio is better), 2-random edges out LRU as the cache gets bigger. The story is similar in the hierarchical case, except that we don't really look at the smaller cache sizes where LRU is superior.
Comparing the two cases, the results are different, but similar enough that it looks our original results weren't only an artifact of looking at the last level of a hierarchical cache.
Below, we'll look at the entire distribution so we can see if the mean of the ratios is being skewed by tiny results.
It looks like, for a particular cache size (one column of the graph), the randomized algorithms do better when miss rates are relatively high and worse when miss rates are relatively low, so, if anything, they're disadvantaged when we just look at the geometric mean — if we were to take the arithmetic mean, the result would be dominated by the larger results, where 2 random choices and plain old random do relatively well
4
.
From what we've seen of the mean ratios, 2-random looks fine for large caches, and from what we've seen of the distribution of the results, that's despite 2-random being penalized by the mean ratio metric, which makes it seem pretty good for large caches.
However, it's common to implement pseudo-LRU policies because LRU can be too expensive to be workable. data.title: Robert Wilson has died
data.author: paulpauper
data.article_summary: 罗伯特·威尔逊（Robert Wilson），这位以实验性戏剧和独特视觉风格闻名的导演兼艺术家，于2025年7月31日去世，享年83岁。在其长达六十年的职业生涯中，他与玛丽娜·阿布拉莫维奇、菲利普·格拉斯、劳瑞·安德森和Lady Gaga等多位艺术家合作，创作了众多风格化的表演和图像。威尔逊以拒绝自然主义的戏剧风格著称，代表作包括《Deafman Glance》（1970）和与菲利普·格拉斯合作的《Einstein on the Beach》（1976）。他的作品常在世界各地的剧院、歌剧院和艺术节上演。此外，他还是一位多产的视觉艺术家，创作了大量绘画、雕塑和装置艺术，并在全球多个博物馆举办展览。威尔逊的《Video Portraits》系列于2013年在卢浮宫展出，其中包括对Lady Gaga、布拉德·皮特等人的肖像创作。他于2011年与玛丽娜·阿布拉莫维奇合作了半自传体舞台剧《The Life and Death of Marina Abramović》。威尔逊生于1941年，在德克萨斯州一个保守的社区长大，他的艺术创作深受早年生活经历的影响。

Artists
news
Robert Wilson, experimental playwright, director and artist, has died, aged 83
Over a six-decade career, he created elegantly stylised performances and images with collaborators including Marina Abramović, Philip Glass, Laurie Anderson and Lady Gaga
Benjamin Sutton
1 August 2025
Share
Robert Wilson at the Watermill Center
Photo: © Bronwen Sharp
Robert Wilson, a visionary artist best known for his highly visual and stylised approach to theatrical performances, has died, aged 83. According to a statement released by the Watermill Center, the arts organisation he founded in Water Mill, New York, Wilson died at his home there on Thursday (31 July) following “a brief but acute illness”.
“While facing his diagnosis with clear eyes and determination, he still felt compelled to keep working and creating right up until the very end,” the statement notes. “His works for the stage, on paper, sculptures and video portraits, as well as The Watermill Center, will endure as Robert Wilson’s artistic legacy.”
Wilson was one of the most critically distinguished and distinctive directors and playwrights of the past half-century. His original productions—including the “silent opera”
Deafman Glance
(1970) and his canonic, epic collaboration with the composer Philip Glass,
Einstein on the Beach
(1976)—are in frequent production at theatres, opera houses and festivals around the world. As are his adaptations of classical works by Bertolt Brecht, William Shakespeare, Samuel Beckett, Virginia Woolf and others.
His works for the stage were known for a stylised dramaturgy that rejected naturalism. They drew on a wide range of musical collaborators from Glass to Tom Waits and Lou Reed, as well as performance modes drawn from silent film, mime and more. Their bold visual aesthetic typically involved sleek, minimalist stages and imaginative uses of lighting and projection.
“I very often stage a work—whether it’s
The Ring
of Wagner or
Hamlet—
visually first, and then later I add text,” he told
The Guardian
in 2022. “The visual book is as important as the audio.”
A scene from a 2012 staging of Robert Wilson and Philip Glass's
Einstein on the Beach
(1976)
Photo © Lucie Jansch
Some of Wilson’s stage projects are also known for their incredibly long durations;
Einstein on the Beach
stretches to nearly five hours, and attendees are encouraged to come and go at their leisure throughout the performance. However, it is positively concise compared to
KA MOUNTAIN AND GUARDenia TERRACE
(1972), which was staged on a mountain in Iran over the course of seven days.
Wilson was also a prolific visual artist, creating drawings, sculptures and other objects to inform and accompany his stage productions; these were the subject of
an exhibition at SFMoMA
in 1991. He has had solo exhibitions or created installations at institutions around the world including the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston; Centre Pompidou in Paris; the Vitra Design Museum in Weil, Germany; the Minneapolis Institute of Art, Mudac Lausanne and many more. He created the exhibition design for the blockbuster Giorgio Armani retrospective that opened at the Solomon R. Guggenheim in New York in 2000 and subsequently travelled for seven years throughout Europe and Asia.
In the 2010s he began creating his
Video Portraits

The Death of Marat
(1793) and Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres’s
Mademoiselle Caroline Rivière
(1793-1807). Those videos were shown alongside an installation of around 700 works from Wilson’s personal collection. Subsequent works in the
Video Portraits
series include portraits of the artists Pope.L and Zhang Huan, as well as the actors Isabella Rossellini, Brad Pitt and Winona Ryder.

The Art Newspaper

44764568.article_summary: 罗伯特·威尔逊（Robert Wilson），这位以实验性戏剧和独特视觉风格闻名的导演兼艺术家，于2025年7月31日去世，享年83岁。在其长达六十年的职业生涯中，他与玛丽娜·阿布拉莫维奇、菲利普·格拉斯、劳瑞·安德森和Lady Gaga等多位艺术家合作，创作了众多风格化的表演和图像。威尔逊以拒绝自然主义的戏剧风格著称，代表作包括《Deafman Glance》（1970）和与菲利普·格拉斯合作的《Einstein on the Beach》（1976）。他的作品常在世界各地的剧院、歌剧院和艺术节上演。此外，他还是一位多产的视觉艺术家，创作了大量绘画、雕塑和装置艺术，并在全球多个博物馆举办展览。威尔逊的《Video Portraits》系列于2013年在卢浮宫展出，其中包括对Lady Gaga、布拉德·皮特等人的肖像创作。他于2011年与玛丽娜·阿布拉莫维奇合作了半自传体舞台剧《The Life and Death of Marina Abramović》。威尔逊生于1941年，在德克萨斯州一个保守的社区长大，他的艺术创作深受早年生活经历的影响。

主要讨论点：C++编译器中的边界检查、安全性强化以及相关技术实现的讨论

不同观点：
• [wyldfire] 认为C++中边界检查的成本已经变得非常低，可以默认启用。他引用了Carruth的博客，指出标准库类型中边界检查仅占0.3%的性能开销，并强调边界检查是强化安全性的重要部分。

• [another_twist] 提出可以向LLVM添加安全的访问指令，通过三阶段更新来实现：首先向LLVM的中间表示（IR）添加指令，然后更新中间代码生成器，最后更新后端支持。这种方式可能比在每种语言中单独处理更为简洁。

• [rurban] 强调需要关闭C11中的Unicode标识符漏洞，这些漏洞会导致同形字攻击。他指出C26没有计划修复这个问题，并认为没有适当安全措施的Unicode标识符应该被禁用。

• [ajb] 认为从长远来看，最好禁止通过命令行标志关闭检查功能，仅允许在个别函数上进行控制。他指出当前的机制并不完善，使用"#pragma diagnostic pop"来恢复设置容易出错，建议使用函数属性来实现更精细的控制。

• [dilawar] 对边界检查模式的用户预期管理提出质疑，认为C++社区过于重视向后兼容性，导致这种模式可能不会被广泛接受。他指出大多数软件包维护者可能不会欢迎这种频繁的编译器版本间代码破坏。

补充讨论：
• 边界检查的成本问题成为讨论中的一个焦点，[wyldfire]认为其成本低廉，而[dilawar]则担心这种变化可能导致兼容性问题。
• 安全性强化措施包括但不限于边界检查，例如[rurban]提到的Unicode标识符安全问题也是强化的一部分。
• 不同技术实现路径的讨论，如[another_twist]提出的LLVM层面的解决方案，展示了多样化的技术思路。
• [ajb]对命令行标志和函数级别控制的讨论，反映了在实现细节上的不同偏好和实践挑战。

data.title: A laundry-folding robot blew up the Internet. We talked to the inventor
data.author: mhb
data.article_summary: 斯坦福大学研究员Aaron Tan发明了一款名为Lume的洗衣折叠机器人，其外形伪装成床头灯，拥有两只机械臂，可以安静地折叠衣物。该机器人的概念视频在网络上爆红，引发了广泛讨论。虽然当前版本只是一个3D渲染和原型，Tan计划将其设计得更加美观和实用。Lume的灵感来自《美女与野兽》中会动的家具，旨在融入家庭环境而不显得突兀。机器人通过摄像头和手臂配合工作，用户可以通过语音或应用程序控制。虽然有人开玩笑问是否能用于成人用途，Tan明确表示Lume不会进行任何形式的触摸或按摩。Lume的目标是让家务在不知不觉中完成，首先解决人们最讨厌的洗衣折叠问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：洗衣折叠机器人的可行性、实用性及技术实现

不同观点：
• 观点一：对洗衣折叠机器人的实用性表示怀疑  
  — 论据1：现有技术无法有效处理不同材质和形状的衣物，例如毛巾和T恤的折叠方式不同，机器人难以应对多样化的衣物。  
  — 论据2：机器人在处理柔软材料时可能存在困难，尤其是衣物容易缠绕或滑落，影响效率。  
  — 例子：有人提到目前市面上的机器人更多专注于硬质物品，如餐具或玩具的整理，而柔软衣物的处理仍是一个技术难题。

• 观点二：看好洗衣折叠机器人的发展潜力  
  — 论据1：随着人工智能和机器学习技术的发展，机器人可以通过不断学习优化折叠不同类型衣物的技巧。  
  — 论据2：自动化技术在家用电器中的应用越来越广泛，洗衣折叠机器人可以作为智能家居的一部分，节省用户时间。  
  — 例子：有评论提到类似技术已经在一些高端家电中实现，如自动叠衣机在日本市场已有初步应用，未来技术进步可能解决当前的局限。

• 观点三：关注成本与市场接受度  
  — 论据1：洗衣折叠机器人的研发和生产成本可能较高，普通消费者难以负担，市场普及难度大。  
  — 论据2：消费者对新技术接受度有限，尤其是中老年群体，可能更倾向于传统的手工折叠方式。  
  — 例子：有人提到类似的高科技产品如自动驾驶汽车，虽然技术先进但市场推广仍面临诸多挑战，洗衣折叠机器人也可能面临同样的问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论点：技术伦理与隐私问题  
  — 有评论担心洗衣折叠机器人配备的摄像头和传感器可能涉及用户隐私问题，尤其是在家庭环境中使用时，如何保障数据安全和隐私成为一个值得关注的问题。  
  — 有人建议在产品设计时加入隐私保护机制，确保用户数据不会被滥用。

• 讨论点：环境影响  
  — 有人提出洗衣折叠机器人可能带来的环境影响，例如能源消耗问题，认为在追求自动化便利的同时，也应考虑产品的环保性能和可持续性。

总结：围绕洗衣折叠机器人的讨论主要集中在实用性、技术可行性、成本与市场接受度等方面，同时涉及隐私保护和环境影响等附加问题。技术乐观派和怀疑论者各执一词，争议焦点在于当前技术能否有效处理多样化衣物及市场推广的现实挑战。

A laundry-folding robot blew up the Internet. We talked to the guy who invented it
Two arms. One bed. Zero back rubs. Stanford researcher Aaron Tan’s bedside lamp-bot folds laundry quietly, beautifully, and without touching you. Yet.
The Lume laundry folding robot at work.
|

By
Zara Stone
Published
Jul. 30, 2025 • 2:46pm
Aaron Tan,
a robotics researcher at Stanford,
this week posted a teaser video introducing Lume, a robot he has been building. In the video, Lume is disguised as a pair of tall bedside lamps, which quietly bend down and extend two robotic fingers that get to work folding laundry.
It’s an impressive display. Also a weird one. And a little freaky. The 31-second clip racked up 3.8 million views within 48 hours. Some people loved it. Others weren’t sure, sharing the video with comments like “
How legit/far along is this?”
and “You could be the
next Tesla
."
Naturally, we were intrigued, so we called Tan to find out, like, what the hell, and when can we get one of these?
An expert in decentralized robot exploration and robot vision language, Tan told us why he built a laundry-folding lamp, how it works, and why it definitely won’t give you a back rub.
This interview has been edited for clarity and length.
Today’s stories straight to your inbox
Everything you need to know to start your day.
Sign up now!
Let’s start with the obvious: Is that video real or AI-generated?
It’s a render, a 3D model that we built to paint a picture of how we think robots can fit into the home. It’s made to look aesthetically pleasing.
So, do you have a real robot?
Yes, we have the physical prototype right now in a garage in San Francisco. The robot is not as slim as it needs to be. We're going to iterate on that to really bring it to this sexy, beautiful design that you see today.
How did this come about?
I recently finished my Ph.D. in robotics at the University of Toronto in Goldie Nejat’s lab, focused on human/robot interaction: how robots coexist with humans in society. I worked with fellow grad student
Angus Fung
, and when we finished, we wanted to keep working together in robotics. They have so many benefits in the home and can unlock so much time for people. So we took a stab at this with Lume.
What gave you the idea for a lamp robotic arm?
This whole thing was inspired by “Beauty and the Beast.” In the movie, the furniture comes alive, right?
Our overall mission is to build robots in a way that blends beautifully into a personal space. Right now, that looks like robotic furniture. Lamps are a great way to hide robotics in plain sight and a great way to put robots into the home without making your home look like a factory.
The Lume will be the first introduction to robots that blend into your home. We wanted it to have a single purpose, and stay out of the way until needed, like a dishwasher.
The initial use case is quite simple: You take your clean laundry in a laundry basket from the dryer, you dump it on the bed, you walk away, watch a movie, or whatever. When you return, the clothes are folded into neat piles, and all you have to do is put it away. The term I use is “ambient robotics,” where robots sort of work in the background, and you don't see them, but your chores get done.
Why did you decide to tackle laundry first?
I hate doing laundry. I absolutely hate doing it. It takes so much time. In 2025, the washing is automated. The drying is automated. Why are we still standing around folding laundry? Laundry is the only chore where you either don't do it or you have to manually do it. There's no alternative solution to make it faster or easier.
We talked to a bunch of people, and we found out that folding laundry consistently was in the top two most annoying chores for everyone.
What was the other most annoying chore?
Cooking.
The Lume robot in lamp mode.
|
Source:
Syncere AI
Walk me through how it works.
There are cameras at the wrist of the robot hand, which is concealed by the lamp hoods. When the robot is not functioning, it operates as a standard floor lamp, and the lamp hood covers both the robot hand and the camera — it acts like a mechanical shutter for privacy and safety. Only when it's activated — via voice controls or an app — does it reveal the camera and robot hand, which then detects laundry and starts folding.
It's very much in the user's control. It's not supposed to be sentient. It's not supposed to be smart. It's not just going to be like, “Hmm, I think it's time I start folding.”
What about “adult” use cases? A lot of people on X pointed out that those are two hands by a bed, after all. Could it be used for other in-bed activities?
No.
Do you think people might still try to hack it for sex?
It would be really hard — they’d need a Ph.D. to hack the lamps.

44776340.article_summary: 斯坦福大学研究员Aaron Tan发明了一款名为Lume的洗衣折叠机器人，其外形伪装成床头灯，拥有两只机械臂，可以安静地折叠衣物。该机器人的概念视频在网络上爆红，引发了广泛讨论。虽然当前版本只是一个3D渲染和原型，Tan计划将其设计得更加美观和实用。Lume的灵感来自《美女与野兽》中会动的家具，旨在融入家庭环境而不显得突兀。机器人通过摄像头和手臂配合工作，用户可以通过语音或应用程序控制。虽然有人开玩笑问是否能用于成人用途，Tan明确表示Lume不会进行任何形式的触摸或按摩。Lume的目标是让家务在不知不觉中完成，首先解决人们最讨厌的洗衣折叠问题。

44765292.article_content:
This Month in
Ladybird
July 2025
Hello friends! July is done. We merged 319 pull requests from 47 contributors.
Welcoming new sponsors
Ladybird is entirely funded by the generous support of companies and individuals who believe in the open web. This month, we’re excited to welcome the following new sponsors:
Scraping Fish
with $5,000
Blacksmith
with high-performance CI infrastructure
We’re incredibly grateful for their support. If you’re interested in sponsoring the project, please
contact us
.
Web Platform Tests (WPT)
As usual, we’ve made some progress on the Web Platform Tests. We’ve added 13,090 passing tests for a new total of 1,831,856.
Google reCAPTCHA passing
There was a long-standing issue with our
postMessage
implementation: if the serialized type had not previously been used in the destination realm, we would fail to reconstruct it. The realm didn’t recognize the type and rejected the message.
This is now fixed, allowing Google reCAPTCHA to pass!
Unfortunately, this only works on
https://www.google.com/
for now, due to a separate unresolved same-origin policy issue.
High refresh rate support
We now detect the refresh rate of the active screen to determine how often web content should be rendered. Previously, rendering was fixed at 60 frames per second.
Websites using
requestAnimationFrame
now render at up to 120Hz on supported hardware. This change also improves the smoothness of scrolling, animations, transitions, and more.
HTTP/3 support
HTTP/3
support was recently added in curl 8.14.0 for users of OpenSSL and
ngtcp2
. Since Ladybird uses the OpenSSL backend with libcurl, this enabled us to support HTTP/3 as well.
We now negotiate HTTP/3 for servers that advertise it via the
Alt-Svc header
.
We also found and reported an issue in curl where
Alt-Svc: clear
was parsed incorrectly. This has since been
fixed in curl 8.15.0.
Trusted Types
Trusted Types is a security feature that helps prevent cross-site scripting (XSS) by locking down injection sinks like
Element.innerHTML
,
HTMLScriptElement.text
, and
HTMLScriptElement.src
. It allows web developers to define policies that control how sanitized content can be created and consumed.
This month, we added initial support for Trusted Types. This includes recognizing policies and enforcing type-safe DOM writes. Further work is ongoing to support more of the spec and improve compliance.
SVG
foreignObject
improvements
The relationship between HTML and SVG is complex. While SVG content can appear in HTML, SVG can also embed arbitrary HTML using the
foreignObject
element.
This month, we made major improvements to how Ladybird handles
foreignObject
. Layout, style resolution, and rendering inside embedded HTML are now much closer to spec behavior, with better integration between the two worlds.
CSS
content: url(...)
We added support for using
content: url(...)
in CSS pseudo-elements such as
::before
and
::after
. This allows authors to insert images via CSS content, matching behavior seen on modern websites.
:state(foo)
and
:unchecked
pseudo-classes
We gained two new pseudo-classes:
:state(foo)
matches a custom element whose states set includes
"foo"
. This allows custom elements to be styled based on internal state, similar to how
:checked
and
:empty
work.
:unchecked
matches elements that are checkable but currently not checked.
These additions improve our compatibility with web components and modern form styling.
Logical property groups
Building on work from
last month
, we now generate the mappings from logical to physical properties at compile time.
Logical and physical properties form groups—for example, the various
margin
properties—and we now take these into account when serializing styles and when modifying them from JavaScript. This improves both CSS fidelity and performance.
Arbitrary substitution functions
This month we rewrote our implementations of
var()
and
attr()
to align with the formal definition of
arbitrary substitution functions
in recent CSS specs. These are functions that return a value to be substituted into the rule before parsing continues.
Our new implementation is more robust, more spec-compliant, and sets us up to support other substitution functions like
if()
and
env()
in the future.
<syntax>
parsing
CSS now allows authors to define the expected syntax for attribute values using the
<syntax>
type. This is used within
attr()
to guide how the value should be parsed.
For example:
color: attr(
data-color
type(<color
>
));
This instructs the parser to interpret the
data-color
attribute as a CSS color. Ladybird now supports
<syntax>
parsing and uses it to improve behavior in CSS Houdini and custom properties.
@property
progress
We’ve had a stub implementation of
@property
for a while. This month, we started fleshing it out.
We now respect the initial value defined in a
@property
declaration and added initial support for
CSS.registerProperty()
. This brings us closer to full Houdini support.
The Web is UTF-16
By definition, strings in Ja

data.title: Life, Work, Death and the Peasant: Family Formation
data.author: Khaine
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是关于前现代农民的婚姻模式，他们是前工业社会中的大多数人口。文章首先回顾了前现代社会的高死亡率，尤其是婴儿、儿童和产妇的死亡率，导致平均预期寿命较低。在这种背景下，婚姻是家庭形成的第一步，且几乎人人都被期望结婚生子。尽管婚姻在不同文化中存在差异，但前现代社会的婚姻普遍率很高。需要注意的是，精英阶层的婚姻模式与农民显著不同，精英往往因为家族联盟和继承需求而更早结婚。文章特别提到，中世纪西欧的普通农民结婚年龄相对较晚，女性约二十多岁，男性则接近三十岁。理解这些婚姻模式对于认识前现代社会的家庭结构至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文章对普通农民的典型定义及其相关社会现象的讨论

不同观点：
• [pyrale] 认为文章写得不错，但过于专注于概括性描述，导致读者从中获得的实际内容较少。他通过引用一个关于美国空军的新闻故事（链接[1]）来类比这种过于泛泛的讨论风格，暗示文章缺乏具体深度。
• [CalRobert] 对文章中提到的传统社会中婚姻和生育的必然性表示关注，并提出一个假设：现代社会低生育率的原因可能是人们不再因为社会压力而必须生育孩子，而是因为个人选择。他还质疑历史上生育孩子更多是社会要求而非个人意愿，并将此与现代低生育率现象联系起来。

补充讨论：
• [pyrale] 通过引用外部链接（[1]）来表达对文章内容缺乏具体性的批评，显示出对深入分析或具体例证的期待。
• [CalRobert] 提到了一个潜在的社会现象，即传统社会中生育和婚姻的必然性与现代社会个人选择之间的对比，并暗示这可能是低生育率的根源。这一观点引发了对社会规范与个人选择之间张力的思考。
• 争议的焦点在于文章是否过于概括，缺乏对具体历史和社会背景的深入探讨，以及传统社会中的生育和婚姻模式是否真的与现代社会的低生育率有直接关系。

44765562.article_content:
Bret Devereaux
Collections
,
The Peasant
August 1, 2025
27 Minutes
This is the first part of the third part of our series (
I
,
II
) discussing the patterns of life of the pre-modern peasants who made up the great majority of all humans who lived in our agrarian past and indeed a majority of all humans
who have ever lived
.
1
Last week, we looked at death, examining the brutal mortality regime of pre-modern societies, typified by extremely high (c. 50%) infant and child mortality, very high maternal mortality and often high male military mortality, which kept life expectancy
at birth
as low as the mid twenties, while life expectancy at adulthood was better – around 50 – but still very low by modern standards.
This week and next, we’ll start working out some of the consequences of this mortality regime, looking at family formation which in these pre-modern agrarian societies means marriage.  While the intense variability of mortality meant that peasant households came in a variety of single- and multi-family forms, pre-modern agrarian societies generally had strict and rigid expectations for marriage: in nearly all of these societies
everyone
got married and was expected to get around to having children
because the community required them
rather than necessarily because they wanted to.
So this week we’re going to look at marriage patterns, particularly the question of age at first marriage.  Then next week, we’re going to turn to the implications those patterns have for child-bearing and child-rearing.
The family and the household were the fundamental institutions of everyday life for pre-modern people, so understanding their structures and assumptions is crucial for understanding the rest of life in these past societies
.
But first, if you like what you are reading, please share it and if you
really
like it, you can support this project on
Patreon
! While I do teach as the academic equivalent of a tenant farmer, tilling the Big Man’s classes, this project is my little plot of freeheld land which enables me to keep working as a writers and scholar. And if you want updates whenever a new post appears, you can click below for email updates or follow me on
Twitter
and
Bluesky
and (less frequently) Mastodon (@bretdevereaux@historians.social) for updates when posts go live and my general musings; I have largely shifted over to Bluesky (I maintain some
de minimis
presence on Twitter), given that it has become a much better place for historical discussion than Twitter.
Email Address
Subscribe!
Marriage, Marriage is What Brings Us Together, Today
Mawwiage, mawwiage is what brings us together, today.
No, I will not apologize for this joke.
We begin with marriage as the first step in
family
formation (though not necessarily
household
formation, as we’ll see).
Whereas the pre-modern mortality regime is broadly consistent over different cultures, marriage patterns (nuptiality) vary significantly
.  Very nearly all human cultures practice something we can identify as marriage, the mostly-permanent pair-bonding of individuals to create a new family (but not necessarily household) unit into which new children are born.  Different cultures, even in the pre-modern world, differ notably on the
rate
of marriage (though it is, in all cases, by modern standards very high, for reasons which will become clear), its
timing
, and the presence or absence of polygamy.
Before we get into those variables though, we need to make a very important point:
we are talking about peasants.
Remember peasants?  This is a post about peasants.
The marriage patterns of high elites in a society are often quite different from the marriage patterns of most of the society

classic example of this

very

everyone

44765562.article_summary: 这篇文章是关于前现代农民的婚姻模式，他们是前工业社会中的大多数人口。文章首先回顾了前现代社会的高死亡率，尤其是婴儿、儿童和产妇的死亡率，导致平均预期寿命较低。在这种背景下，婚姻是家庭形成的第一步，且几乎人人都被期望结婚生子。尽管婚姻在不同文化中存在差异，但前现代社会的婚姻普遍率很高。需要注意的是，精英阶层的婚姻模式与农民显著不同，精英往往因为家族联盟和继承需求而更早结婚。文章特别提到，中世纪西欧的普通农民结婚年龄相对较晚，女性约二十多岁，男性则接近三十岁。理解这些婚姻模式对于认识前现代社会的家庭结构至关重要。

data.title: Writing a good design document
data.author: kiyanwang
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了如何撰写优秀的设计文档。设计文档是一份技术报告，旨在根据权衡和限制条件，说明系统的实施策略。其目标是让读者相信该设计在给定情况下是最优的，而最需要说服的其实是作者本人。撰写过程有助于澄清模糊的想法，揭示思维中的漏洞。

文档的组织至关重要，应避免写成“意大利面条式”的杂乱无章。好的文档应让读者感觉顺理成章，毫无意外。为此，作者需预见并解决可能的异议，引导读者从当前认知到达认同设计的目标。

编辑时应尽量简化文字，删除不必要的词句，以节省读者注意力。多加练习是关键，像亚马逊这样的公司有浓厚的文档文化，有助于提升写作能力。具体技巧包括使用短段落，将文档视作连贯的要点序列。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：设计文档的目标和最佳实践

不同观点：
• [nickm12] 认为设计文档的目标不是追求最优方案，而是提供足够的解决方案。他强调设计是在约束和权衡之间做出选择，文档应清楚地展示这些选择，并说明为何选择某一方案而非其他替代方案。他不认为设计能消除所有潜在问题，但应尽量降低风险并与利益相关者有效沟通。

• [patrickmay] 强调设计文档的重要性，引用"Writing is nature's way of telling us how sloppy our thinking is"来表明写作有助于澄清思路。他推荐了一篇关于如何提升技术写作质量的文章，并认为即使在行业内多年的人也常常忽视设计文档的重要性。

• [B-Con] 作为设计审查者，认为设计文档应简化复杂问题，不应包含所有困难和错误的细节。他主张文档应使复杂事物简单化，并将不必要的细节放到附录中。

• [farkin88] 指出设计文档批准后可能面临的维护问题，建议使用轻量级的架构决策记录（ADRs）来跟踪上下文和决策状态，以防止设计文档随着时间推移失效。

• [mtlynch] 对亚马逊会议中让参与者在会上阅读文档的做法提出质疑，认为这浪费了宝贵的会议时间。他认为文档应在会前阅读，会议应专注于讨论。

• [ryanmadden] 强调文档的组织和清晰度是软件工程师提升文档写作能力的主要障碍，并讨论了段落长度和信息密度的问题。他分享了自己在谷歌的经验，并提到不同公司可能有不同的文档写作实践。

• [Scarblac] 询问是否有好的设计文档集合，表示在其职业生涯中很少见到优秀的设计文档。

• [cadamsdotcom] 提出使用LLM（大语言模型）来帮助文档写作，建议通过多次简化和修改来提高文档质量。

• [lastdong] 强调通过技术写作课程提高了总结文档的能力，提倡使用“红色笔”方法来减少不必要的词语，并指出这是一项需要定期训练的技能。

• [norseboar] 认为有些读者只想知道结论而不关心推理过程，因此文档应先给出结论以满足这些读者的需求。

• [codemac] 介绍了两种文档结构方法：B.O.O.（背景、目标、概述）和Good Strategy/Bad Strategy（问题诊断、指导方针/假设/需求、行动），并指出不同方法适用于不同情境。

• [kator] 分享了在亚马逊工作7.5年的经验，强调从客户需求出发撰写PRFAQs并收集反馈，即使在个人项目中也坚持这种做法。

• [matt-p] 提到有时会为自己编写设计文档，认为这种方式非常有效，并希望能看到示例文档以作比较。

• [alphazard] 强调在有写作和设计文化的公司工作的重要性，认为工程师应优先选择有书面计划的项目，并避免没有书面计划的领导和项目。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：设计文档是否应包含所有细节还是仅给出结论。例如，[B-Con] 和 [norseboar] 对文档应包含多少细节有不同看法。
• 实用建议：包括使用LLM帮助文档写作（[cadamsdotcom]），通过技术写作课程提升能力（[lastdong]），以及使用ADRs维护文档（[farkin88]）。
• 文档结构和风格：不同评论者提出了多种文档结构和写作风格的建议，如B.O.O.方法（[codemac]）和Good Strategy/Bad Strategy方法（[codemac]）。

总体来看，讨论围绕设计文档的目的、内容、结构和写作技巧展开，参与者分享了各自的经验和建议。

44779428.article_content:
How to write a good design document
This essay is a version of
the response
I gave to my friend Vik's call for suggestions:
had a lot of people ask how they can learn to write design docs, and i didn’t have a good answer besides “work at a place with writing culture and smart senior engineers”. anyone have more useful advice?
https://t.co/7F9BV31shv
— vik (@vikhyatk)
August 31, 2024
Definition
A design document is a technical report that outlines the implementation strategy of a system in the context of trade-offs and constraints.
Goal
Think of a design document like a proof in mathematics. The goal of a proof is to convince the reader that the theorem is true. The goal of a design document is to convince the reader the design is optimal given the situation.
The most important person to convince is
the author
. The act of writing a design document helps to add rigor to what are otherwise vague intuitions. Writing reveals how sloppy your thinking was (and later, code will show how sloppy your writing was).
Organization
Good design document organization is as important as code organization. You probably have opinions about code organization. You've probably used the phrase "spaghetti code" to describe poorly-organized code. Most programmers write "spaghetti design docs" unless they've had a lot of practice.
Let me illustrate a common code organization issue some programmers run into on their first day. The novice writes
terminal.print("Hello world")
Then they decide they want to make the text red, so they edit their program to
terminal.print("Hello world")
terminal.setPrintColor("red")
And then they're confused that it didn't come out red. They haven't internalized that the first line of code
happens before
the second. They just get a soup of code on the screen that kind of has the ingredients for a program, and expect the computer to do what they want.
Novice document writers make the
exact
same mistake, but with prose instead of code. They get a soup of sentences and paragraphs and expect the reader's brain to do what they want.
If the reader is smart enough, you might actually get away with this. Just like an expert programmer can mentally untangle spaghetti code.
But a perfect doc is written such that the reader
is never surprised
. The reader should find that every sentence flows obviously from the previous ones. They should finish your doc and think "well this was entirely straightforward, why did we even need to have this meeting?".
This disappoints the ego-seeking behavior of many engineers. Good engineers often want people to realize how clever they were.
But a good doc will lay out the problem and mental models in a way that the solution that took weeks of hard thought to invent will be clear to the reader by the time the doc presents it.
This also requires having a good model of the minds of the people reading your doc. The goal of your doc is to take their minds from their current state to a new state in which they believe your design is a good one.
You should anticipate every objection someone would have and preemptively show why it's invalid, so that the reader never even thinks to bring it up.
Many engineers fail at modeling the starting state of their readers' minds, so fail at getting them to the destination state.
Editing
Once you've got the information organized and laid out properly, the next step is to edit for length. Remove every word that can be removed. Do this because your readers' attention is a scarce resource.
Unless you're an unusually terse writer, you can almost always cut length by ~30% from the first draft without sacrificing information.
The easiest way to get good at editing by going through
other
people's docs with a red pen and crossing out unnecessary words. You'll find tons. It's easier to criticize other people.
Once you've built this muscle, you can turn the weapon on yourself. Distilling thoughts to fit into the 280 character tweet limit is also surprisingly good practice.
Volume
There's no substitute for lots of practice. I'm grateful for having worked at AWS with a unique doc-writing culture. The first docs I wrote there were terrible, but after a few hundred, I like to think they were pretty good.
For unfamiliar readers: Amazon meetings start with the presenter passing out copies (historically physical, though increasingly digital since Covid) of a prose document. The document is 1-6 pages depending on the importance.
The meeting starts with everyone sitting in silence, reading the document, and adding notes and questions in the margins with red pen. Watching people mark up the document you spent so much time polishing is a
strong
forcing function to become a better writer.
Concrete tips
These work for me, but they may not work for you.
Use short paragraphs
You should think of your doc as a series of bullet points that flow into each other. That is, a doc might be organized like:
Observation A
Observation B
Because B, idea C
But problems D and E
Observation F
Ther

data.title: This Old SGI: notes and memoirs on the Silicon Graphics 4D series (1996)
data.author: exvi
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是A. J. Corda编写的关于修复和维护SGI 4D系列机器的经验笔记，包含系统安装、硬件配置、故障排查等详细信息。主要内容包括：不同SGI系统的配置与性能、图形设置、串口连接、电源问题、实时时钟与非易失性内存问题、音频能力、硬件调试技巧等。此外，文章还介绍了如何绕过NVRAM密码、恢复格式化磁盘、构建可引导的IRIX文件系统等技术细节。作者提到，通过Usenet获取信息的重要性，并建议在未收到回复时重新审视问题，而不要急于重新发布帖子。文章旨在分享作者的经验，回馈网络社区的帮助。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对老旧高性能工作站（如SGI系列）与现代设备的比较与讨论，以及对硬件接口和电源等技术细节的交流。

不同观点：
• **Lastdong** 认为，由于Nvidia的进步，现在普通人在家就能拥有以前像SGI级别的高性能机器。他提到了Hacker News上的一个相关讨论，暗示技术进步使得曾经的高端设备变得更普及。

• **Fidotron** 分享了自己获得一台罕见的老式4D/60 "buttons box"的经历，强调了老设备与现代设备在接口和兼容性上的问题。他还提到以前拥有Indigo工作站的经历，指出老设备在与现代设备连接时存在困难。此外，他提到一位前VR公司的CTO对电力供应的关注，暗示在高端计算设备运行中电源问题的重要性。

• **T1234s** 简单表达了对O2工作站设计上的赞赏，尤其是其组件易于更换的特点。

• **JSR_FDED** 回忆了自己修复一台在火灾中受损的Indigo2 Max Impact的经历，并强调了该工作站曾经的高价值。同时，他认为IRIX 4Dwm桌面系统在今天仍然具有竞争力。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个老式高性能工作站（如SGI的4D/60、Indigo、O2和Indigo2 Max Impact），用户们分享了这些设备的技术特点、历史价值以及在现代使用中的局限性和挑战（如电源、接口兼容性）。
• 争议的焦点并不明显，但存在对老设备在现代使用中的实用性不同看法。Lastdong和Fidotron似乎更关注现代技术进步如何替代老设备，而JSR_FDED和T1234s则表现出对老设备的情感和对其技术特点的赞赏。
• Fidotron还提到了电源问题，特别是高性能设备对电力供应的高要求，这为讨论增加了一个技术细节层面的关注点。

I am posting this assortment of notes and observations as
a kind of "thank you" to the numerous people who have replied
to my posts in the past.  The free flow of information is
the life-blood of the internet community, and this is my feeble
attempt to maintain that flow, while at the same time repaying
the kindness shown me by other members of the community in my
rather obsessive attempts to revive a defunct 4D professional
series machine.
I have posted a number of messages concerning my project, and
I can say that all the replies I have received have been quite
helpful. One of the things you learn early on as a denizen of
the net is the utility of Usenet posts. You also learn that
the volume of answers can convey almost as much information
as the content of those answers. If I post a question and
receive a significant number of replies, then I can be relatively
certain that others have run across (and possibly solved) the
same class of problem. If, however, I receive no responses, it
indicates that this is a new problem not previously encountered

the problem represents a true hardware-level failure (usually
at the IC level) or the problem is due to some fundamental stupidity
on my part (by far the most likely scenario!). This means that
it's time to re-evaluate the procedure which caused the problem,
which usually leads to an alternate approach which inevitably
works. During this project, I have only had 2 genuine hardware

it was at last evident that this was not a common bug.

44779178.article_content:
Environment and sustainability
New global study shows freshwater is disappearing at alarming rates
ASU-led research uses 20 years of satellite data to reveal unprecedented continental drying
Earth’s continents have experienced unprecedented freshwater loss since 2002, driven by climate change, unsustainable groundwater use and extreme droughts. A new ASU-led study highlights the emergence of four continental-scale “mega-drying” regions, all located in the Northern Hemisphere, with staggering implications for freshwater availability. Image by Sophia Franz
By
Sandy Keaton Leander
|
July 25, 2025
New findings from studying over two decades of satellite observations reveal that the Earth’s continents have experienced unprecedented freshwater loss since 2002, driven by climate change, unsustainable groundwater use and extreme droughts.
The study, led by Arizona State University and published today in
Science Advances
, highlights the emergence of four continental-scale “mega-drying” regions, all located in the Northern Hemisphere, and warns of severe consequences for water security, agriculture, sea-level rise and global stability.
The research team reports that drying areas on land are expanding at a rate roughly twice the size of California every year. And, the rate at which dry areas are getting drier now outpaces the rate at which wet areas are getting wetter, reversing long-standing hydrological patterns.
The negative implications of this for available freshwater are staggering. Seventy-five percent of the world’s population lives in 101 countries that have been losing freshwater for the past 22 years. According to the
United Nations
, the world’s population is expected to continue to grow for the next 50 to 60 years — at the same time the availability of freshwater is dramatically shrinking.
The researchers identified the type of water loss on land, and for the first time, found that 68% came from groundwater alone — contributing more to sea level rise than glaciers and ice caps on land.
Jay Famiglietti
“These findings send perhaps the most alarming message yet about the impact of climate change on our water resources,” said
Jay Famiglietti
, the study’s principal investigator and a Global Futures Professor with the ASU
School of Sustainability
.
“Continents are drying, freshwater availability is shrinking, and sea-level rise is accelerating. The consequences of continued groundwater overuse could undermine food and water security for billions of people around the world. This is an ‘all-hands-on-deck’ moment — we need immediate action on global water security.”
The researchers evaluated more than two decades of data from U.S.-German Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and GRACE-Follow On (GRACE-FO) missions, looking at how and why terrestrial water storage has changed since 2002. Terrestrial water storage includes all of Earth’s surface and vegetation water, soil moisture, ice, snow and groundwater stored on land.
Hrishikesh A. Chandanpurkar
“It is striking how much nonrenewable water we are losing,” said Hrishikesh A. Chandanpurkar, lead author of the study and a research scientist for ASU.
“Glaciers and deep groundwater are sort of ancient trust funds. Instead of using them only in times of need, such as a prolonged drought, we are taking them for granted," he said. "Also, we are not trying to replenish the groundwater systems during wet years and thus edging towards an imminent freshwater bankruptcy.”
Tipping point and worsening continental drying
The study identified what seems to be a tipping point around 2014–15 during a time considered “mega El-Niño” years. Climate extremes began accelerating and in response, groundwater use increased and continental drying exceeded the rates of glacier and ice sheet melting.
Additionally, the study revealed a previously unreported oscillation where after 2014, drying regions flipped from being located mostly in the Southern Hemisphere to mostly in the north, and vice versa for wet regions.
One of the key drivers contributing to continental drying is the increasing extremes of drought in the mid-latitudes of the Northern Hemisphere, for example, in Europe. Additionally, in Canada and Russia, snow, ice and permafrost melting increased over the last decade, and the continued depletion of groundwater globally is a major factor.
This figure shows the long-term terrestrial water storage trends from GRACE/FO averaged for every country (Feb 2003–April 2024).
In a
previous study
, members of the team studied terrestrial water storage from satellite data spanning 2002–2016. In the new study, the team looked at more than 20 years of data and discovered a critical, major development in continental drying. Several regional drying patterns and previously identified localized "hot spots" for terrestrial water storage loss are now interconnected — forming the four continental-scale mega-drying regions.
These include:
Southwestern North America and Central America
: Thi

data.title: Modern Node.js Patterns
data.author: eustoria
data.article_summary:
Node.js经历了显著变革，从以回调和CommonJS为主的旧模式转变为基于现代Web标准的开发方式。以下是2025年Node.js的关键变化：

1. **模块系统：ESM成为新标准**  
   过去使用的CommonJS模块系统已被ES Modules（ESM）取代。ESM支持更好的工具链和静态分析，且与浏览器标准一致。Node.js现在使用`node:`前缀明确标识内置模块，避免依赖冲突，如：
   ```javascript
   import { add } from './math.js';
   import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
   ```

2. **顶层Await：简化初始化**  
   无需再用 async 函数包裹整个应用，顶层await让初始化代码更简洁：
   ```javascript
   const config = await readFile('config.json', 'utf8');
   ```

3. **内置Web API：减少外部依赖**  
   Node.js引入了Fetch API等Web标准API，减少对外部库的依赖。例如，原生支持HTTP请求、超时和取消操作：
   ```javascript
   const response = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data');
   const data = await response.json();
   ```

4. **AbortController：优雅取消操作**  
   通过AbortController可以优雅地取消长时间运行的操作，处理超时或用户取消请求：
   ```javascript
   const controller = new AbortController();
   setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 10000);
   ```

这些变化提高了Node.js的一致性、可维护性和开发体验。

主要讨论点：Node.js 新特性及其与竞争者（如Deno、Bun）的对比

不同观点：
• simonw 认为 Node.js 引入的文件系统和网络访问限制是一个受 Deno 启发的优秀特性，提供了更强的安全性。
• farkin88 强调了 Node 核心内置 fetch 和 AbortController 的重要性，指出这减少了对外部库（如 axios）的依赖，从而优化了性能，特别是在 Lambda 函数冷启动场景下。
• jmull 对 "Modern Event Handling with AsyncIterators" 部分的代码示例提出质疑，认为存在遗漏，可能是复制粘贴错误或AI生成内容的问题。

• austin-cheney 将新特性分为两类：新技术和已有功能的“美化层”，并指出开发者对这两类的优先级选择值得关注。

• growbell_social 对 Node.js 重新在 Hacker News 等平台获得关注表示高兴，特别是在 2012-2018 年间一度被忽视的背景下。

• 多位评论者提到了 Node 与其他 JS 运行时（如 Deno 和 Bun）的竞争关系，认为这种竞争推动了 Node 的进步。

44778936.article_summary:
Node.js经历了显著变革，从以回调和CommonJS为主的旧模式转变为基于现代Web标准的开发方式。以下是2025年Node.js的关键变化：

1. **模块系统：ESM成为新标准**  
   过去使用的CommonJS模块系统已被ES Modules（ESM）取代。ESM支持更好的工具链和静态分析，且与浏览器标准一致。Node.js现在使用`node:`前缀明确标识内置模块，避免依赖冲突，如：
   ```javascript
   import { add } from './math.js';
   import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
   ```

2. **顶层Await：简化初始化**  
   无需再用 async 函数包裹整个应用，顶层await让初始化代码更简洁：
   ```javascript
   const config = await readFile('config.json', 'utf8');
   ```

3. **内置Web API：减少外部依赖**  
   Node.js引入了Fetch API等Web标准API，减少对外部库的依赖。例如，原生支持HTTP请求、超时和取消操作：
   ```javascript
   const response = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data');
   const data = await response.json();
   ```

4. **AbortController：优雅取消操作**  
   通过AbortController可以优雅地取消长时间运行的操作，处理超时或用户取消请求：
   ```javascript
   const controller = new AbortController();
   setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 10000);
   ```

这些变化提高了Node.js的一致性、可维护性和开发体验。

不同观点：
• [ahmedfromtunis] 认为军事装备的年龄不直接等同于过时，五十年前的装备在今天可能仍然有效。例如，学习如何操作这些老旧设备依然具有现实意义。

• [empiko] 强调中国在造船方面远远超过美国，每年建造的船只数量是美国的200倍，暗示中国军事能力的快速扩张及其潜在影响。

• [jleyank] 对大规模运输的需求提出质疑，认为目前大多数军事力量通过海运或空运投送，除了重型弹药外，未必需要大幅增加运输能力。

• [staplung] 指出美国许多军事装备已经老化，例如尼米兹号航母服役已达50年，B-52轰炸机设计更早，A-10攻击机和一些枪械也使用了数十年，暗示需要更新。

• [6yyyyyy] 提出是否需要维持海外军事基地和运输能力的问题，建议关闭所有海外基地以节省开支。

data.title: Watching the World in a Dark Room: The Early Modern Camera Obscura
data.author: prismatic
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了早期现代人们对暗箱（camera obscura）的迷恋及其带来的奇妙体验。暗箱作为摄影技术的前身，是一个黑暗房间或盒子，通过一个小孔让外界图像倒映在室内墙壁上，产生梦幻般的效果。这种设备被科学家、艺术家和诗人用于研究光学、观察自然现象和娱乐。亚里士多德最早记录了类似现象，而像Giambattista della Porta等自然哲学家则详细描述了如何利用暗箱制造出内外颠倒的奇妙影像。暗箱不仅提供了视觉上的奇观，还带有一种精神层面的启示，类似于中世纪通过黑暗感知神光的理念。暗箱通过遮蔽光线，创造了一个转换和幻象的空间，揭示了光与暗的复杂关系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Camera obscura的历史应用及其现代体验

不同观点：
• **[历史应用及艺术影响]**  
  - **staplung** 认为，Camera obscura 早在1500年代可能就被欧洲的一些画家使用，例如Vermeer、达·芬奇和Hans Holbein等艺术家。虽然证据稀少，但有一些特征性畸变表明了其使用痕迹。作者还分享了现代艺术家Abelardo Morell使用该技术拍摄的图片和一段使用都铎时代camera obscura进行肖像实验的视频。
  
• **[个人体验]**  
  - **thenthenthen** 分享了自己住在简陋房屋时的亲身经历，提到因为没有光，通过一个小孔洞看到了类似“摄影”的投影图像，认为这种体验非常“诗意”。尽管这种现象可能与墙面结构有关，但这种偶然的视觉效果让他联想到电影颗粒感。
  
• **[旅游体验及变化]**  
  - **JKCalhoun** 描述了自己二十年前在苏格兰参观爱丁堡Camera Obscura的经历，认为当时的体验很酷，但最近一次故地重游发现它变成了一个以家庭和儿童为主的体验场所，因而选择了不参与。这表明Camera obscura作为旅游景点的功能和定位发生了变化。

• **[流行文化中的应用]**  
  - **1659447091** 提到在AMC的电视剧《Snowpiercer》中有一个Camera obscura场景，被剧中人物用于“电影时间”，这展示了该技术在现代流行文化中的再现和应用。

补充讨论：
- Camera obscura 作为一种古老的光学设备，其历史应用引发了关于其在艺术史中具体影响的讨论。
- 不同用户分享了各自的亲身经历和现代的camera obscura体验，从个人观察到旅游景点再到流行文化，展现了该设备在不同背景下的多样化应用。
- **争议焦点**：Camera obscura在艺术史中的实际应用范围和影响仍然存在争议，因为证据有限，学术界对其具体使用者（如Vermeer等艺术家）的怀疑尚未消除。

Watching the World in a Dark Room
The Early Modern Camera Obscura
By
Julie Park
Centuries before photography froze the world into neat frames, scientists, poets, and artists streamed transient images into dark interior spaces with the help of a camera obscura. Julie Park explores the early modern fascination with this quasi-spiritual technology and the magic, melancholy, and dream-like experiences it produced.
Published
July 31, 2025
Scroll through the whole page to download all images before printing.
“Athanasius Kircher’s camera obscura”, illustration from Kirscher’s
Ars magna lucis et umbrae
(1671) reproduced in Josef Maria Eder’s
Ausführliches Handbuch der Photographie
(Detailed handbook of photography, 1905) —
Source
.
The camera obscura, a device known as the photographic camera’s predecessor, was originally the size of a room. As an artist’s aid for rendering perspective, a scientific model for understanding optics, and a source of popular entertainment, it furnished observers with all kinds of information during the early modern period. In the context of pursuing knowledge about the natural world — whether in studying the sun, the light it emits, or the very organ for seeing, the eye — alchemists, astronomers, and mathematicians turned rooms in their homes into camera obscuras for revealing what was previously invisible.
In the most rudimentary terms, the camera obscura (whose Latin name means “dark chamber”) is a dark and enclosed environment with a hole on one side. This aperture allows light to stream into the interior space, casting moving images onto the opposite wall. Because its images of external reality appear reversed, both laterally and vertically — in colors deeper than their original, with movements intact but seemingly exaggerated — the camera obscura’s projections of the world re-envision it as a dream.
One of the very first mentions of the phenomenon behind the camera obscura is tied to the viewing of a solar eclipse.
1
Aristotle, while observing a partial solar eclipse in the fourth century BCE, glimpsed its reflection in the play of light that seeped through the dense canopy of a tree. Here, the “dark chamber” is not a box or a room, but the critical space between solid things. Transposing this phenomenon onto the walls of domestic architecture, early modern natural philosophers made it possible to experience the domain of one’s personal space as a realm of marvelous reversal and illusion.
Scroll through the whole page to download all images before printing.
First published image of a camera obscura, from Gemma R. Frisius’
De radio astronomico et geometrico liber
(1545) —
Source
.
Scroll through the whole page to download all images before printing.
Frontispiece to James Ayscough’s
A Short Account of the Eye and Nature of Vision
(1755) —
Source
.
For Giambattista della Porta, polymath author of
Natural Magic
(1558), a book of natural philosophy and alchemy filled with magic tricks and scientific experiments, the camera obscura was a space for “see[ing] all things in the dark, that are outwardly done in the Sun, with the colours of them”.
2
This evocative phrasing suggests the metaphysical happenings that the experience of being and peering inside a camera obscura offers. Della Porta’s instructions for engineering this “very pleasant and admirable” experience — among the “great secrets of Nature” — involve managing sources of light and creating the conditions by which it can be strategically channeled: “you must shut all the Chamber windows, and it will do well to shut up all holes besides”, except for one that is as wide and long as your hand.
3
By covering the walls with paper or white cloth to create a viewing screen, the outside world will appear indoors, both familiar and estranged: “so shall you see all that is done without in the Sun, and those that walk in the streets, like to Antipodes, and what is right will be the left, and all things changed.”
4
A spiritual dimension inheres in this experience: the notion of illumination via obscuration that surrounds the early modern camera obscura carries remnants of the medieval period’s approach to darkness as the medium for perceiving the glorious light of God. Elina Gertsman explains how nowhere was this more evident than in windows through which light, both colored and clear, flooded into the darkness of cathedrals.
5
Without the dimly lit cathedral space, this transmission of light as an expression of God’s splendor would not be so keenly felt. Both cathedrals and camera obscuras share the principle that dark places form the critical environment through which transformative light and its effects can be channeled. Yet in the case of camera obscuras, it was not just light alone, but ever more wondrous projections of the world that illuminated enclosed spaces.

data.title: ChatGPT chats were indexed then removed from search but still remain online
data.author: Growtika
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了ChatGPT的聊天内容因分享功能被公开索引，导致超过10万条聊天记录在Google等搜索引擎上可被检索，其中包含敏感信息如简历、商业计划和个人隐私。尽管OpenAI迅速采取措施，添加"noindex"和"nofollow"标签并请求谷歌移除链接，但这些内容已被互联网档案馆保存且无法轻易删除。文章还讨论了用户隐私保护、数据所有权和公共分享功能的责任问题，提醒用户注意此类工具的潜在风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI的分享功能及其引发的隐私问题

不同观点：
• Sweepi认为问题出在用户没有理解“允许在网络搜索中显示”的选项，而不是OpenAI的错。他指出选项描述已经很清楚，用户误解是自身问题。
• Simple10提到DuckDuckGo仍然索引了很多分享链接，特别是文件上传的链接，包含了财务和市场分析等内容。他还指出发现了包含个人身份信息（PII）的求职申请分享，包括姓名、电话号码和地址等。
• Ufko_org的观点是，如果用户无法理解共享聊天将会公开访问，那是用户自身的问题，和AI无关。
• iJohnDoe认为Internet Archive本可以做正确的事，移除这些数据，尽管现在可能已经移除。
• Fardo认为这应该是一个不具争议的话题，选项描述已经足够清楚，任何具备基本阅读理解能力的用户都应该能明白。他认为更多警告是浪费时间，问题在于用户自身。
• J45质疑为什么这些链接没有显示404错误。
• _Cs2017_提问，在修复后，“可发现”选项设置了nofollow/noindex，那么现在“可发现”和“不可发现”的聊天有什么区别。
• SoftTalker提醒大家，任何在网络表单中输入的内容都有可能公开展现，因此要保持谨慎。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对用户误解选项和隐私泄露问题存在争议。一部分人认为是用户自身问题，另一部分人则关注具体隐私泄露的实例，如PII泄露。
• 讨论还涉及到技术细节，如nofollow/noindex的作用以及为什么某些链接仍然可以访问。
• 争议焦点在于责任归属问题：是用户误解还是平台设计不够完善。

ChatGPT Chats Were Indexed Then Removed From Search but Still Remain Online
ChatGPT Chats Were Indexed Then Removed From Search but Still Remain Online
By:
Growtika
Updated: 2 August 2025
What started as a sharing feature turned into an unexpected SEO exposure. Over 100,000 ChatGPT chats were publicly accessible, some indexed, and many archived long before OpenAI responded.
Table of Contents
Toggle
It all started with something simple: a “Share” button
When OpenAI let people share ChatGPT conversations publicly, it probably felt like a helpful feature. You click, get a clean link, and show off a cool prompt or funny exchange.
But tucked behind that button was a small checkbox. “Make this chat discoverable” And that changed everything.
People clicked without fully thinking it through. And just like that, thousands of ChatGPT chats ended up in Google search results. These weren’t private links anymore. They were public pages, visible to anyone. Some were harmless. Many were not.
Some chats revealed resumes and job applications. Others included internal business plans, sensitive political views, confessions of cheating on academic work, or deeply personal struggles. Real names were attached. Real people were exposed. And for a moment, all of it was searchable on Google.
Tahir Naqash
shared in a tweet that even API keys and developer prompts were showing up in search results.
Any ChatGPT chats shared via link are publicly accessible on Google, Bing and other search engines.
— Dozens of chat with sensitive data, personal information, important codes are now “indexed” on search engines.
pic.twitter.com/hZiu7QmmJB
— Tahir Naqash 🥑 (@Naqashfeed)
August 1, 2025
Pete Sena
illustrated the issue in real time, sharing Google searches that surfaced deeply personal ChatGPT conversations directly from OpenAI’s domain.
Everyone said I was paranoid about AI privacy.
I just proved them wrong.
Copy these into Google RIGHT NOW:
– site:
https://t.co/WHqbr8BY0B
“my startup failed”
– site:
https://t.co/WHqbr8BY0B
“I’m addicted to”
– site:
https://t.co/WHqbr8BY0B
“please don’t tell anyone”
-…
pic.twitter.com/MBceaqXTrF
— Pete Sena (@petesena)
July 31, 2025
Fast Company
caught it early
. SEO folks and digital sleuths found even more.
OpenAI moved quickly.
They added
noindex
and
nofollow
tags to shared chat pages and asked Google to remove them. And credit where it’s due, Google responded. Tens of thousands of links disappeared from search results.
OpenAI’s Chief Information Security Officer
confirmed on X
that the feature had been removed.
We just removed a feature from
@ChatGPTapp
that allowed users to make their conversations discoverable by search engines, such as Google. This was a short-lived experiment to help people discover useful conversations. This feature required users to opt-in, first by picking a chat…
pic.twitter.com/mGI3lF05Ua
— DANΞ (@cryps1s)
July 31, 2025
But the damage was already done.
Because Google isn’t the only place where information lives. By the time OpenAI fixed the indexing issue, a massive chunk of those shared chats had already been saved by the Internet Archive.
More than 100,000 of them, according to researchers
Henk van Ess
and
Nicolas Deleur
. Archived in full. Searchable. Permanent.
ChatGPT quietly scrubbed today nearly 50,000 shared conversations from Google’s index after our investigation. They thought they’d solved the problem. They were wrong. (1/5)
pic.twitter.com/cNE7UJdTCd
— 𝚑𝚎𝚗𝚔 𝚟𝚊𝚗 𝚎𝚜𝚜 (@henkvaness)
August 1, 2025
And here’s the kicker: Archive.org says OpenAI hasn’t asked for any of them to be removed.
Mark Graham, the director of the Internet Archive,
responded
to van Ess’s inquiry by saying that if OpenAI requested the removal of chatgpt.com/share URLs, they would likely honor it. But so far, OpenAI hasn’t made that request.
That opens up a mess of questions:
Who actually owns a ChatGPT conversation once it’s shared?
Should OpenAI protect users who didn’t fully realize what they were sharing?
What if some users
do
want their chats preserved? Whose rights matter more?
And maybe the biggest question of all:
Should we really be rolling out public sharing features without making people understand what they’re exposing?
Even now, OpenAI’s
robots.txt
file technically still lets search engines access
/share/*
. That no longer leads to indexing because of the new meta tags, but it’s a reminder of how easy it is to overlook details that can expose real people.
This isn’t a hit piece on OpenAI. The truth is more complicated. We’re all playing catch-up with the speed of these tools. ChatGPT makes it easy to forget that what feels like a private conversation can, with a single click, become a published page.
That’s what happened here. People didn’t think “Share

• iJohnDoe认为Internet Archive本可以做正确的事，移除这些数据，尽管现在可能已经移除。
• Fardo认为这应该是一个不具争议的话题，选项描述已经足够清楚，任何具备基本阅读理解能力的用户都应该能明白。他认为更多警告是浪费时间，问题在于用户自身。
• J45质疑为什么这些链接没有显示404错误。
• _Cs2017_提问，在修复后，“可发现”选项设置了nofollow/noindex，那么现在“可发现”和“不可发现”的聊天有什么区别。
• SoftTalker提醒大家，任何在网络表单中输入的内容都有可能公开展现，因此要保持谨慎。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对用户误解选项和隐私泄露问题存在争议。一部分人认为是用户自身问题，另一部分人则关注具体隐私泄露的实例，如PII泄露。
• 讨论还涉及到技术细节，如nofollow/noindex的作用以及为什么某些链接仍然可以访问。
• 争议焦点在于责任归属问题：是用户误解还是平台设计不够完善。

data.title: 6 weeks of Claude Code
data.author: mike1o1
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了使用Claude Code工具在过去六周内对编程工作的巨大影响。Claude Code帮助作者大幅提升了代码编写的效率和自由度，使他可以在处理其他任务的同时，快速完成大量技术任务，如将React Native组件转换为React、迁移数据库模型、重写iOS启动系统等。这些任务原本属于技术债务，通常需要大量时间处理，但现在通过Claude Code可以轻松完成。作者认为，这种变化类似于摄影技术引入时的变革，编程方式将发生根本性转变。尽管LLMs（大语言模型）可能带来社会问题，但其对编程的影响不可逆转。作者还强调了“先写后决定”的新工作习惯，鼓励在行动前先尝试想法。总体而言，Claude Code显著降低了维护成本，改变了作者对技术债务的处理方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Claude Code的使用体验和价值

不同观点：
• **支持并赞赏Claude Code**：
  - **lukaslalinsky**：有超过25年编程经验，认为Claude Code尽管有学习曲线，但表现出色，尤其在提供上下文和分块任务时。曾尝试Gemini CLI但体验不佳，正考虑升级Claude Code的付费计划。
  - **jeswin**：Claude Code远超其他工具，尤其在AI代码生成方面。强调好的规格说明、测试和类型的重要性，并分享了使用技巧。
  - **arrowsmith**：Claude Code不仅能写代码，还能通过CLI工具控制整个计算机，完成诸如图片处理和音频编辑等任务，极大地节省时间。
  - **buffer1337**：分享了使用Claude Code的技巧，如更换到sonnet模式和有效管理Docker容器，极大提升了工作效率。
  - **lysecret**：有10年经验，认为Claude Code消除了开始编码的痛苦，能专注于思考和分析，并能同时处理多个任务。
  - **d4rkp4ttern**：Claude Code帮助完成了之前不敢尝试的任务，如HTML日志和Pydantic版本迁移，显著提升了工作效率。

• **质疑和批评Claude Code**：
  - **Fraterkes**：作为初级开发者，担心使用Claude Code会失去学习和提升编码能力的机会，存在内心矛盾。
  - **actinium226**：认为解释任务所需时间与自己完成任务的时间差不多，未感受到显著效率提升。
  - **acedTrex**：经常因Claude Code的速度慢和错误而感到沮丧，感觉不可靠，尤其在转换shell配置时遇到问题。

• **中立和比较**：
  - **minzi**：质疑Claude Code是否比Cursor的代理工具更好，特别是两者都使用sonnet的情况下，不愿花费额外费用尝试。

补充讨论：
• **对编码的反思**：
  - **philbo**：尽管许多人赞赏Claude Code，但自己更喜欢手工编码，认为编码如同绘画，仍有其独特的乐趣和价值。
  - **slackpad**：Claude Code降低了维护和重构的激活能量，但需谨慎使用，以免导致倦怠和积累技术债务。
  - **softwaredoug**：Claude Code带来的不是生产力提升，而是更深入的思考和研究，帮助避免未来的后悔。

• **争议焦点**：
  - **使用Claude Code是否剥夺学习机会**：Fraterkes担心依赖工具会失去学习机会，而支持者认为工具能提高效率和思考深度。
  - **工具的可靠性和效率**：部分用户如acedTrex和actinium226对Claude Code的可靠性和效率提出质疑，而其他用户如lukaslalinsky和lysecret则高度赞赏其效率和功能。

通过这些讨论，可以看出Claude Code在提升效率、辅助编码任务方面有显著优势，但也存在学习曲线、可靠性和个人成长方面的争议。

44746621.article_content:
It is wild to think that it has been only a handful of weeks.
Claude Code has considerably changed my relationship to writing and maintaining code at scale. I still write code at the same level of quality, but I feel like I have a new freedom of expression which is hard to fully articulate.
Claude Code has decoupled myself from writing every line of code, I still consider myself fully responsible for everything I ship to Puzzmo, but the ability to instantly create a whole scene instead of going line by line, word by word is incredibly powerful.
I believe with Claude Code, we are at the
“introduction of photography”
period of programming. Painting by hand just doesn’t have the same appeal anymore when a single concept can just appear and you shape it into the thing you want with your code review and editing skills.
If this feels like an intimidating line-of-thought then welcome to the mid-2020s, nothing is stable anymore and change is the only constant. Sorry. I didn’t make it so nearly all of culture’s changes are
bad
, and I think that LLMs are already doing social damage and will do much worse in the future - but this genie is fully out of the bottle and it is substantially going to change what we think of as programming.
A Retrospective on the last 6 Weeks
#
This article builds on
“On Coding with Claude”
which I wrote after using Claude for a week. If you think that I am AI-pilled, you can get my nuanced take on LLMs at
the start
of that post.
That said, this is transformative and I want to try give you some perspective from the last 6 weeks of activity in the Puzzmo engineering space to try and show you what I’ve been seeing.
Maintenance is Significantly Cheaper
#
I have been on many projects with people which have taken weeks full-time to perform some sort of mundane task: “converting this JS codebase to TypeScript”, “Update to Swift X”, “Switch to a monorepo” they’re the kind of things which are delicate migrations which require a gazillion rebases.
Here is a list of things which I have completed,
solo
, since getting access to Claude Code:
Converting hundreds of React Native components to just React
Replaced 3 non-trivial RedwoodJS systems with home-grown or mature, supported replacements
Built complex REPLs for multiple internal and external projects
Switched almost every db model to have a consistent ‘flags’ system for booleans
Converted from Jest to Vitest
Created our front-end testing strategies for React
Moved many things defined in code to run via the CMS
Made significant headway on server-side rendering
Re-wrote the iOS app’s launch system due to deprecations
Built a suite of LLM created (and framed as such, hen hand annotated) documentation for systems like leaderboards, dailies etc
Converted a significant amount of our design system primitives to use base-ui
Migrated significant code from inline styles to stylex
Converted all animations in puzzmo.com to use the same techniques as games
Fixed multiple bugs which have been around since the start of Puzzmo
Updated all Vite integrations
Migrate all Puzzmo production projects to node 22
Convert the games repo to a real monorepo
Built iPad support for the Puzzmo app
None of these projects are the “actual work” which I need to do on a day to day basis as the ‘bizdev’ guy on Puzzmo for this year. These are
literally side-projects
which I did
on my own
while working on something else.
For clarity in the back because this is shocking to me, while I was still working on the existing roadmap I had prior to Claude Code over the last 6 weeks, I accomplished all of these things on my own. Mostly in the background (and then with a polish pass day for some of the larger ones). I didn’t go from working ~10 hour days to working ~16 hours or anything like that either.
This was years of
“tech debt” / “tech innovation”
backlog for me! Done in just over a month and a half.
If you understand what you are doing, the capacity for building and handling the breadth of tasks which typically live within the remit of “technical debt”
do not need to be treated as debt
and you can just do it as you are working on other things.
‘carving out some time on the schedule’
is now so incredibly cheap that getting started and making a serious dint is
something you can prime before going into a meeting
, then deciding if you thought it was the right thing after. Mind-blowing.
Write First, Decide Later
#
A habit I have been trying to form is to give an idea a shot before I fully shoot it down. For example, since day 1 on Puzzmo I had been waiting on figuring out a testing strategy for the front-end because I wanted to be able to hire someone to fully own “puzzmo.com” and a part of that is figuring out how to not do as many regressions as we get.
Figuring out a testing strategy for the front-end isn’t pretty, and I have seen a lot of really bad test suites which over-test and become brittle things that engineers don’t like to work with. The mix of networking, react, the scope of contex

data.title: Show HN: Turn impulse buys into dream investments
data.author: pjcodes
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过不同的心理和工具策略来控制和反思消费行为

不同观点：
• echoangle认为"成本重构"（将价格转换为工作小时数）虽然能让人更清楚地意识到交易的代价，但反而可能促使他更愿意购买那些他认为只需要很少工作时间就能获得的物品。他还对示例中的收入和计算方式提出质疑，怀疑示例中的工资水平过低或未考虑全额收入。

• iJohnDoe提出了一个关于自动储蓄和还债的应用想法，建议将类似于"四舍五入"的储蓄机制用于偿还信用卡债务。他认为即使是小额的自动还款也能产生积极效果，并强调该应用需要具备直接支付信用卡的功能以提高效率。

• dsaltzman支持在成本重构和目标重定向的基础上，增加显示"当前金额在5/10年后的增长价值"的功能，以帮助用户更长远地考虑消费决策，尤其是与大额支出（如首付）相关的决策。

• nihiven对如何触发该应用的功能表示疑问，特别提到一个检测冲动购买的场景。他质疑是否能在冲动购买时自动触发应用提醒，而不是依赖用户手动打开应用来阻止自己。他关注的是应用如何在购买过程中引入"摩擦"以减少冲动消费。

• LorenDB则认为没有必要为了将价格除以自己的时薪而专门使用一个完整的网络应用，暗示这种功能可能过于简单，不值得专门开发一个应用。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及到如何通过技术和心理策略来帮助用户更好地控制消费行为，如自动储蓄、债务偿还、冲动购买检测等。
• 争议的焦点在于应用的实际效果和触发机制，尤其是如何有效减少冲动购买以及用户是否愿意手动使用这些工具。
• 不同的功能需求和改进建议，如显示未来增长价值和直接支付信用卡，显示出用户对消费管理工具的多样化需求。

data.title: Australian state seeks to enshrine work from home in law
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary: 维多利亚州州长Jacinta Allan宣布计划将居家工作写入法律，确保员工每周至少有两天可以居家工作（如果工作性质允许）。该政策旨在提高工作效率，节省家庭开支和时间，并帮助更多女性留在职场。Allan表示，这项变化将赋予符合条件的员工每周两天居家工作的权利，并预计能为每位员工每周节省约110澳元。该政策将与员工、雇主和工会进行磋商，并可能在明年提交州议会审议。反对党领袖也表示支持促进工作与生活平衡的措施。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于远程工作法规是否能有效激励远程工作模式

不同观点：
• **支持法规的立场**：评论者对政治家承认远程工作的好处表示欢迎，并希望能够通过政策激励远程工作，或者至少不加以限制。评论者认为远程工作具有积极意义，期待政策能推动这一趋势。

• **对法规可能产生反效果的担忧**：评论者担心法规设定的最低标准和豁免条款可能会导致企业为了避免遵守复杂标准而干脆完全禁止远程工作。这样一来，原本可能允许远程工作的企业，会因为难以满足法规要求而选择直接不允许员工远程工作，从而适得其反。

补充讨论：
• **法规设计问题**：评论者指出了法规设计中的潜在漏洞，即通过设置过高的门槛，可能无意中促使企业选择更为保守的策略，完全避免远程工作以减少合规成本或麻烦。

• **豁免条款的负面影响**：豁免条款原本可能是为了应对无法实现远程工作的特殊情况，但评论者认为这可能会成为企业规避远程工作要求的便捷途径，进而导致远程工作机会减少。

争议焦点：
• 法规是否能真正促进远程工作，还是可能因设计不当而适得其反。具体而言，最低标准的设定和豁免条款的应用是争议的核心。

Under Jacinta Allan's plan, workers would be entitled to work from home at least two days per week, if the job allows.
Photo:
123rf
The premier of the Australian state of Victoria announced Saturday plans to enshrine working from home in law, saying it should be "a right, not a request".
Under Jacinta Allan's plan, workers would be entitled to work from home at least two days per week, if the job allows.
"We're doing that because we know what the evidence tells us - workers are more productive, it saves time for families, it saves money for families," Allan said, launching the proposed policy at the Labor Party's state conference.
"This change will mean that any worker who can reasonably do their job from home has the right to do so for at least two days a week."
Allan said the policy would now go out for consultation with workers, employers and unions.
She said it was important to "get the details of this important change right".
Allan said the move could save the average worker A$110 (NZ$120) a week, cut congestion on roads, and keep more women in the workforce.
During national elections in May, the opposition Liberal-National coalition's plan to eliminate remote work was partly blamed for its poor performance.
Victoria's Opposition leader, Brad Battin, said work from home arrangements had been valuable, and that he supported measures that promote better work-life balance.
The measure is likely to come before the state Parliament next year.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI研究人员获得高额薪酬的现象及其合理性

不同观点：
• 支持高薪酬的观点：
  - AI研究人员的稀缺性和潜在巨大影响力使得高薪合理。例如，顶级AI研究员可能带来的技术和商业价值远超其高薪成本，类似于顶级运动员的高薪（[meekaaku]）。
  - 这些高薪酬反映了AI领域竞争的激烈和人才的稀缺，公司愿意支付高额薪酬以确保获得最优秀的人才（[apparent], [BSOhealth]）。
  - 高薪酬可以通过股票等非现金形式支付，对于预期增长的公司来说，这是一种合理的激励手段（[Voultapher]）。

• 质疑高薪酬的观点：
  - 有人质疑这些高薪酬是否合理，特别是如果AI研究人员最终只能带来边际收益（[joshdavham]）。
  - 有人担心这些高薪酬可能是一种“炒作”，公司支付高额薪酬以吸引人才，但这些人才是否能带来相应的回报尚不确定（[TheAceOfHearts], [fidotron]）。
  - 高薪酬的结构（如股票期权）可能存在风险，如果公司股票表现不佳，这些薪酬可能变得不值钱（[missedthecue], [ghushn3]）。

• 对高薪现象的态度和感受：
  - 有人对这种高薪现象感到不满，认为这会给亲友带来不必要的压力，要求他们也去大公司工作（[habosa]）。
  - 有人对这种现象感到不解，不明白为什么有人愿意为了高薪而放弃自己的创业梦想，去为大公司工作（[ghushn3]）。

补充讨论：
• 有人提到这种高薪现象是“赢家通吃”经济的结果，类似于娱乐明星和体育明星的高薪（[apparent], [BSOhealth]）。
• 有人认为这种高薪现象可能意味着Meta对AGI（人工智能通用智能）的预期提前，反映了对未来技术突破的竞争（[thom]）。
• 讨论中还涉及到对合同细节和工作要求的疑问，例如这些高薪研究员是否需要在公司办公室长时间工作，以及他们的工作是否会带来预期的成功（[TheAceOfHearts]）。

总体而言，讨论围绕AI研究人员高薪现象的合理性、动机以及潜在风险展开，参与者从不同角度提出了支持和质疑的观点。

data.title: The Dollar Is Dead
data.author: nhp_fermi
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美元作为全球储备货币的地位是否会衰退，以及可能的影响和替代方案。

不同观点：
• **逻辑链条的可靠性**：[regnull] 认为，尽管每个推理步骤看似合理，但整个逻辑链条的总体可靠性会下降。即使每一步都有90%的可能性，整个链条的可能性也会大大降低。
• **历史分析与帝国兴衰**：[Luker88] 引用Ray Dalio的书，通过历史分析多个帝国的兴衰，指出中国崛起和美国衰退的趋势，但强调文化差异和货币储备角色的重要性，认为权力更替可能需要更长时间。
• **政治与经济无能**：[Workaccount2] 认为美国国会无法有效管理经济问题，导致通胀不可避免，最终美元会被迫贬值以减轻债务负担。
• **全球力量对比**：[dustingetz] 质疑弱势美元的叙述，指出欧洲和中国的经济问题，并认为美国科技行业的优势依然明显。
• **替代货币的可能性**：
  - [declan_roberts] 认为没有任何外国货币或货币篮可以替代美元，美元崩溃将拖垮全球经济。
  - [etempleton] 认为缺乏可信的替代货币，可能需要复杂的货币指数，但政治信任度低。
  - [kesor] 认为 fiat 货币依赖信任，失去信任时无需替代货币，通过Gresham's Law自然消亡。

补充讨论：
• **全球保护主义与多极化**：[nhp_fermi] 提出，如果全球变得更加保护主义，可能不需要单一的全球储备货币，而是出现多个区域储备货币。
• **债务投资的现实性**：[daft_pink] 认为在低利率环境下，不投资长期债务是正常现象，而利率回归5-10%是向现实的回归。
• **加密货币与美元的主导地位**：[dlcarrier] 观察到，尽管有加密货币等新技术，美元在世界贸易中的主导地位依然通过稳定币表现出来。
• **个人投资与信念**：[Esophagus4] 强调通过个人投资行为来验证对经济预测的信心，而不仅仅是言论。

争议焦点：
• **美元衰退的必然性与速度**：一部分人认为美元衰退不可避免且正在发生，另一部分人则认为美元仍具有不可替代性，衰退过程可能更缓慢或复杂。
• **替代货币的可行性**：关于是否有其他货币或货币体系可以替代美元，评论中存在明显分歧。

data.title: AI hallucinations will be solvable within a year (2024)
data.author: rvz
data.article_summary: 前谷歌AI研究员Raza Habib在伦敦的Fortune Brainstorm AI会议上表示，AI幻觉问题有望在一年内解决。AI模型在训练过程中会经历预训练、微调和基于人类反馈的强化学习三个阶段，目前模型在微调前已经表现出良好的校准能力。Habib认为，解决AI幻觉问题只是如何在提高模型可控性的同时保留其校准能力。不过，他同时指出，不完全解决这一问题也可能接受，因为AI偶尔的“幻觉”可能有助于提出新颖的想法，特别是在创意任务中。此外，Habib还批评了Air Canada的聊天机器人事故，认为是缺乏充分测试和防护措施所致。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）的“幻觉”问题（即模型生成不准确或虚假信息）及其可能的解决方案

不同观点：
• [davesmylie] 认为，自文章发布以来，LLM的幻觉问题不仅没有减少，反而变得更加普遍。他以自身经验为例，指出自己越来越容易察觉到模型在编造信息，这可能是因为对LLM的使用经验增加了。

• [ipv6ipv4] 持相对悲观的观点，认为幻觉问题是无法根治的，因为即使是人类智能的最佳现有模型（即人类自身）也存在类似问题。他的论据是，人类本身也会产生幻觉或错误认知，因此幻觉问题在LLM中可能是不可避免的。

• [techpineapple] 提出了一个不同的思路，讨论是否应该追求一个“完美”的LLM来解决问题，还是使用五个有意偏向的LLM。这暗示了对LLM设计和应用策略的探讨，可能认为多样性和偏向性在某些场景下有其优势。

• [d00mB0t] 没有直接讨论技术问题，而是批评讨论中的某些人（可能是某些专家或权威人士）自以为是地向大众说教。他的评论反映了一种对讨论态度或方式的不满，而不是对LLM技术本身的直接评价。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于LLM幻觉问题是否可以解决或减轻。一方认为问题越来越严重，另一方认为幻觉是固有的、无法根治的问题。
• [techpineapple] 提出的关于“完美LLM”和“多个偏向LLM”的讨论引入了一种新的视角，即在某些情况下，多个有偏向的模型可能比一个完美的模型更有用，这为LLM的实际应用提供了新的思路。
• [d00mB0t] 的评论虽然不涉及具体技术问题，但反映了讨论中的一种情绪，即对专家意见的不满或怀疑，这可能是讨论中的一个潜在张力点。

总结：评论中关于LLM幻觉问题的讨论涉及了问题的严重性、是否可以解决以及可能的应用策略。观点多样，从技术性讨论到对讨论方式的批评，展现了多角度的思考。

AI hallucinations will be solvable within a year, ex-Google AI researcher says—but that may not be a good thing: ‘We want them to propose things that are weird and novel’
By
Orianna Rosa Royle
By
Orianna Rosa Royle
Associate Editor, Success
Orianna Rosa Royle
Associate Editor, Success
Orianna Rosa Royle is the Success associate editor at
Fortune
, overseeing careers, leadership, and company culture coverage. She was previously the senior reporter at
Management Today
, Britain's longest-running publication for CEOs.
SEE FULL BIO
Raza Habib, cofounder and CEO, Humanloop, at Fortune Brainstorm AI London on April 16, 2024.
Joe Maher—Fortune Brainstorm AI
If you’ve ever asked ChatGPT, Gemini, and other generative AI chatbots a question, you’ll have found that the answers they throw out can be fascinating at best—or completely made up, at worst.
But you won’t need to worry about AI hallucinating for much longer. That’s because AI experts told
Fortune
that the phenomenon is “obviously solvable” and they’ve estimated that will happen soon.
“I’m optimistic that we can solve it,” Raza Habib, who went from
Google
AI research intern to founding Humanloop in less than six months, revealed on a panel at the Fortune Brainstorm AI conference in London.
“When you train a large language model, it goes through three stages—there’s pre-training, fine-tuning, and then reinforcement learning from human feedback as the last stage,” Habib explained.
His London-based startup, which has
raised $2.6 million
, pioneered methods to make the training of large language models, such as those that underpin OpenAI’s ChatGPT, more efficient.
“If you look at the models before they are fine-tuned on human preferences, they’re surprisingly well calibrated. So if you ask the model for its confidence to an answer—that confidence correlates really well with whether or not the model is telling the truth—we then train them on human preferences and undo this.
“So the knowledge is kind of there already,” Habib added. “The thing we need to figure out is how to preserve it once we make the models more steerable.
“But the fact that the models are learning calibration in the process already makes me very optimistic that it should be much easier to solve.”
A year, but…
When pressed for how long this will take, Habib responded: “Within a year.”
But he doesn’t think it needs to be solved because we are so used to clunky tech anyway.
“We’re used to designing user experiences that are fault-tolerant in some way,” the UCL graduate, who has a Ph.D. in machine learning, added. “You go to Google search, you get a ranked list of links, you don’t get an answer, and people who are in Perplexity get citations back now.
“So I don’t think it has to be solved to make it useful.”
Plus, Habib thinks that a little bit of hallucination could be good—necessary even—if we want AI to help humanity think outside of the box.
“If we want to have models that will one day be able to create new knowledge for us, then we need them to be able to act as conjecture machines; we want them to propose things that are weird and novel—and then be able to filter that in some way,” he explained.
“So in some senses, [especially] if you’re doing creative tasks, having the models be able to sort of fabricate things that are going off the data domain is not necessarily a terrible thing.”
Last year, Habib was among around 20 software developers and startup CEOs to attend a closed-door meeting with Sam Altman. At the time, OpenAI’s
recently reinstated
cofounder and CEO told the collective his plans for the company, including how it’s coping with chip shortages—and Habib came under fire for
leaking the entire conversation in a blog post.
Air Canada chatbot mishap ‘completely avoidable’
The panel—made up of Habib, ServiceNow’s VP of AI product Jeremy Barnes, and Rebecca Gorman, cofounder and CEO of Aligned AI—also debated Air Canada’s chatbot mishap.
If you’re unfamiliar with the story: Jake Moffatt bought an Air Canada ticket to go to the funeral of his grandmother in 2022. The company’s AI chatbot convinced the customer to buy a full-price ticket on the premise that he’d retroactively be able to get a partial refund under its reduced bereavement fare policy.
So Moffatt bought full-price tickets from Vancouver to Toronto for about $590 and then a few days later paid $630 to return.
But when he requested some money back, Air Canada said the chatbot was wrong. Now, Canada’s main airline has been ordered to pay the customer compensation—but the entire situation was, in Habib’s eyes, “completely avoidable.”
“I just don’t think that they had done enough around testing,” he said, adding that the airline at least should have “had sufficient guardrails in place.”

data.title: Show HN: Structured Cooperation – A new way of building distributed apps & POC
data.author: gabrielshanahan
data.article_summary: 该仓库包含Scoop，一个结构化协作的概念验证实现，适用于分布式、基于消息的系统。结构化协作是一套服务在分布式系统中遵守的规则，旨在解决传统分布式系统中难以推理、调试、管理错误和资源的问题。Scoop通过制定一套规则来确保操作的顺序性和一致性，例如在处理"账户创建"和"合同创建"消息时，确保操作按正确顺序执行，并有效处理错误。该项目使用Kotlin编写，基于Postgres构建自定义消息系统，但规则具有通用性，可用于不同语言和技术栈。Scoop类似于编排库（如Temporal），帮助开发者在分布式系统中编写业务操作。
